title.zh: 卷三百九十四 列傳第一百五十三 胡紘 何澹 林栗 高文虎 陳自強 鄭丙 京鏜 謝深甫 許及之 梁汝嘉
title.en: Volume 394 Biographies 153: Hu Hong, He Dan, Lin Li, Gao Wenhu, Chen Ziqiang, Zheng Bing, Jing Tang, Xie Shenfu, Xu Jizhi, Liang Rujia
title.raw: 卷三百九十四 列傳第一百五十三 胡紘 何澹 林栗 高文虎 陳自強 鄭丙 京鏜 謝深甫 許及之 梁汝嘉 Volume 394 Biographies 153: Hu Hong, He Dan, Lin Li, Gao Wenhu, Chen Ziqiang, Zheng Bing, Jing Tang, Xie Shenfu, Xu Jizhi, Liang Rujia

sentences.zh: 胡紘，字應期，處州遂昌人。

translations.literal: Hu Hong, styled Yingqi, was a man of Suichang in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Hong, whose courtesy name was Yingqi, came from Suichang in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the Chunxi era he was raised as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunxi period he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 紹熙五年，以京鏜薦，監都進奏院，遷司農寺主簿、秘書郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxi, on Jing Tang's recommendation, he supervised the Directorate for Court Memorials, then was transferred to Registrar of the Ministry of Revenue and Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1194, recommended by Jing Tang, he was appointed supervisor of the Directorate for Court Memorials and later promoted to registrar in the Ministry of Revenue and secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄用事，逐朱熹、趙汝愚，意猶未快，遂擢紘監察御史。

translations.literal: When Han Tuozhou held power he drove out Zhu Xi and Zhao Ruyu, yet was still not satisfied, and so promoted Hong to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Tuozhou seized power and expelled Zhu Xi and Zhao Ruyu, he was still not content and therefore elevated Hong to the post of investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 紘未達時，嘗謁朱熹于建安，熹待學子惟脫粟飯，遇紘不能異也，紘不悅，語人曰：「此非人情。

translations.literal: Before Hong had attained office, he once called on Zhu Xi at Jian'an; Xi treated students only with husked grain, and toward Hong made no exception; Hong was displeased and said to others, 'This is not human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had risen to office, Hong had once visited Zhu Xi at Jian'an. Xi served his students nothing but plain grain, and he treated Hong no differently. Hong took offense and told others, "This is hardly how one treats a guest.

sentences.zh: 隻雞尊酒，山中未為乏也。」

translations.literal: A single chicken and a cup of wine are not lacking in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: A chicken and a cup of wine are not scarce in the hills."

sentences.zh: 遂亡去。

translations.literal: He thereupon left and went away.
translations.idiomatic: With that he departed and never returned.

sentences.zh: 及是，劾趙汝愚，且詆其引用朱熹為偽學罪首。

translations.literal: At this time he impeached Zhao Ruyu and moreover slandered him for employing Zhu Xi as chief of the crime of false learning.
translations.idiomatic: Now he impeached Zhao Ruyu and denounced him for promoting Zhu Xi as the ringleader of so-called false learning.

sentences.zh: 汝愚遂謫永州。

translations.literal: Ruyu was thereupon demoted to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu was accordingly banished to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 汝愚初抵罪去國，搢紳大夫與夫學校之士，皆憤悒不平，疏論甚眾。

translations.literal: When Ruyu first incurred guilt and left the state, gentry officials and scholars of the schools were all resentful and indignant, and memorials of protest were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruyu first fell from grace and left the capital, court officials and academy scholars alike were indignant, and protests poured in from every side.

sentences.zh: 侂胄患之，以汝愚之門及朱熹之徒多知名士，不便於己，欲盡去之，謂不可一一誣以罪，則設為偽學之目以擯之。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was troubled by this; because Ruyu's followers and Zhu Xi's disciples included many famous scholars inconvenient to himself, he wished to remove them all; saying they could not all be framed with crimes one by one, he set up the label of false learning to exclude them.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou found this troubling. Ruyu's circle and Zhu Xi's followers included many eminent men who stood in his way, and he wanted them all gone. Since he could not charge each one individually, he invented the category of "false learning" to drive them out.

sentences.zh: 用何澹、劉德秀為言官，專擊偽學，然未有誦言攻熹者。

translations.literal: He employed He Dan and Liu Dexiu as remonstrance officials to attack false learning exclusively, yet there was none who openly assailed Xi in speech.
translations.idiomatic: He installed He Dan and Liu Dexiu as censors to specialize in attacking false learning, but no one had yet spoken openly against Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 獨紘草疏將上，會改太常少卿，不果。

translations.literal: Hong alone drafted a memorial about to be submitted, but on being transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hong alone drafted a memorial ready for submission, but he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices before it could be sent.

sentences.zh: 沈繼祖以追論程頤得為察官，紘遂以藁授之。

translations.literal: Shen Jizu, by reviling Cheng Yi, obtained appointment as censor; Hong thereupon gave him the draft.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jizu won a censor's post by reviling Cheng Yi, and Hong handed him the draft.

sentences.zh: 繼祖論熹，皆紘筆也。

translations.literal: Jizu's attacks on Xi were all Hong's writing.
translations.idiomatic: Every word of Jizu's indictment of Xi came from Hong's pen.

sentences.zh: 寧宗以孝宗嫡孫行三年服，紘言止當服期。

translations.literal: Emperor Ningzong, as legitimate grandson of Emperor Xiaozong, observed three years of mourning; Hong said he should observe only one year.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ningzong, as Xiaozong's legitimate grandson, was observing three years of mourning. Hong argued that he need observe only one year.

sentences.zh: 詔侍從、臺諫、給舍集議釋服，於是徙紘太常少卿，使草定其禮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered attendant officials, censors, and drafting officials to assemble and discuss ending mourning; thereupon Hong was moved to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to draft the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered attendant officials, censors, and drafting officers to deliberate on ending mourning, and Hong was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to draft the ritual.

sentences.zh: 既而親饗太廟。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he personally offered sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor personally sacrificed at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 紘既解言責，復入疏云：「比年以來，偽學猖獗，圖為不軌，動搖上皇，詆誣聖德，幾至大亂。

translations.literal: Hong, having been relieved of remonstrance duty, again submitted a memorial saying: 'In recent years false learning has run rampant, plotting irregular conduct, shaking the retired emperor, slandering the sage virtue, nearly reaching great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: After Hong left his censorial post, he submitted another memorial: "In recent years false learning has run wild, plotting sedition, unsettling the retired emperor, and defaming the throne—nearly bringing the realm to chaos.

sentences.zh: 賴二三大臣、臺諫出死力而排之，故元惡殞命，群邪屏跡。

translations.literal: Thanks to two or three great ministers and censors exerting their utmost to repel it, the chief villain perished and the host of evils vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Only because a few great ministers and censors fought with all their strength were the chief culprits destroyed and their followers driven off.

sentences.zh: 自御筆有『救偏建中』之說，或者誤認天意，急於奉承，倡為調停之議，取前日偽學之姦黨次第用之，以冀幸其他日不相報復。

translations.literal: Since the imperial brush had the saying 'correcting bias and establishing the mean,' some mistakenly took it as Heaven's intent and, eager to flatter, advocated compromise, taking the former false-learning factionaries and employing them in turn, hoping that later they would not retaliate.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor's own brush had spoken of "correcting bias and establishing the mean," some mistook this for divine approval and rushed to flatter him by urging reconciliation—reappointing the old false-learning faction one by one in the hope they would not seek revenge later.

sentences.zh: 往者建中靖國之事，可以為戒，陛下何未悟也。

translations.literal: The affair of Jianzhong and Jingguo in the past may serve as a warning—why has Your Majesty not yet understood?
translations.idiomatic: The Jianzhong and Jingguo period should be warning enough. Why has Your Majesty not yet seen it?

sentences.zh: 漢霍光廢昌邑王賀，一日而誅群臣一百餘人；

translations.literal: In Han, Huo Guang deposed King He of Changyi and in one day executed more than a hundred ministers;
translations.idiomatic: When Huo Guang deposed King He of Changyi, he executed more than a hundred courtiers in a single day.

sentences.zh: 唐五王不殺武三思，不旋踵而皆斃于三思之手。

translations.literal: In Tang the Five Princes did not kill Wu Sansi, and before they could turn around all perished at Sansi's hands.
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Princes of Tang failed to kill Wu Sansi, they were all dead at his hands almost at once.

sentences.zh: 今縱未能盡用古法，亦宜且令退伏田里，循省愆咎。」

translations.literal: Now even if the ancient method cannot be fully used, they should at least be made to withdraw and lie low in the countryside, examining their faults.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we cannot follow the ancients entirely, these men should at least be sent back to the countryside to reflect on their errors."

sentences.zh: 俄遷紘起居舍人。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Hong was transferred to Drafting Attendant of the Privy Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hong was promoted to drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 詔偽學之黨，宰執權住進擬，用紘言也。

translations.literal: An edict on the false-learning faction suspended the chief ministers' authority to advance nominations—this followed Hong's words.
translations.idiomatic: An edict barred the chief ministers from advancing members of the false-learning faction, following Hong's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 自是學禁益急。

translations.literal: From this the ban on learning grew stricter.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the proscription of learning grew harsher still.

sentences.zh: 進起居郎，權工部侍郎，移禮部，又移吏部。

translations.literal: He advanced to Attendant of the Privy Secretariat, acting Vice Minister of Works, then was transferred to Rites and again to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant of the privy secretariat, then served as acting vice minister of works before transfers to the ministries of rites and personnel.

sentences.zh: 坐同知貢舉、考宏詞不當而罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for misconduct as associate examiner of the metropolitan examination and examiner of the Hongci examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for irregularities while serving as associate examiner of the metropolitan examination and grader of the Hongci literary competition.

sentences.zh: 未幾，學禁漸弛，紘亦廢棄，卒於家。

translations.literal: Before long the learning ban gradually relaxed; Hong too was cast aside and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the learning ban eased, Hong was cast aside as well, and he died at home.

sentences.zh: 何澹，字自然，處州龍泉人。

translations.literal: He Dan, styled Ziran, was a man of Longquan in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Dan, courtesy name Ziran, was a native of Longquan in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年進士，累官至國子司業，遷祭酒，除兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Qiandao, he rose through offices to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, then Director, and was appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1166, he rose through the ranks to vice director and then director of the Directorate of Education before appointment as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 光宗內禪，拜右諫議大夫兼侍講。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong abdicated internally, he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong abdicated in favor of his son, Dan was appointed right remonstrance grandee and concurrent lecturer.

sentences.zh: 澹本周必大所厚，始為學官，二年不遷，留正奏遷之，澹憾必大，及長諫垣，即劾必大，必大遂策免。

translations.literal: Dan had been favored by Zhou Bida; at first as academic official he was not promoted for two years; Liu Zheng memorialized for his promotion; Dan resented Bida, and when he headed the remonstrance bureau he immediately impeached Bida, and Bida was removed by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had once enjoyed Zhou Bida's patronage. As an academic official he went two years without promotion until Liu Zheng intervened on his behalf. Dan resented Bida, and once he headed the censorate he impeached him, driving Bida from office.

sentences.zh: 澹嘗與所善劉光祖言之，光祖曰：「周丞相豈無可論，第其門多佳士，不可並及其所薦者。」

translations.literal: Dan once spoke of this to his friend Liu Guangzu; Guangzu said: 'Chancellor Zhou surely has faults worth discussing, only his gate has many fine scholars—one cannot lump together those he recommended.
translations.idiomatic: Dan once discussed this with his friend Liu Guangzu, who said, "Chancellor Zhou surely has faults worth airing, but his circle includes many worthy men. You cannot condemn everyone he recommended along with him.

sentences.zh: 澹不聽。

translations.literal: Dan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Dan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時姜特立、譙熙載以春坊舊恩頗用事。

translations.literal: At the time Jiang Teli and Qiao Xizai, by old favor from the Eastern Palace, were rather influential.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jiang Teli and Qiao Xizai wielded considerable influence through their old ties to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 一日，光祖過澹，因語澹曰：「曾、龍之事不可再。」

translations.literal: One day Guangzu visited Dan and said to him: 'The affairs of Zeng and Long must not be repeated.
translations.idiomatic: One day Guangzu visited Dan and said, "What happened with Zeng and Long must not happen again.

sentences.zh: 澹曰：「得非姜、譙之謂乎？」

translations.literal: Dan said: 'You cannot mean Jiang and Qiao?
translations.idiomatic: Dan replied, "You mean Jiang and Qiao, do you not?"

sentences.zh: 既而澹引光祖入便坐，則皆姜、譙之徒也，光祖始悟澹謾諾。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Dan led Guangzu into an informal seat, and they were all followers of Jiang and Qiao; Guangzu then realized Dan's empty assent.
translations.idiomatic: Then Dan ushered Guangzu into a side room where Jiang's and Qiao's men were gathered, and Guangzu realized Dan's agreement had been hollow.

sentences.zh: 明年，澹同知貢舉，光祖除殿中侍御史，首上學術邪正之章。

translations.literal: The next year Dan was associate examiner; Guangzu was appointed Palace Attendant Censor and first submitted a memorial on orthodox and heterodox learning.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, as Dan served as associate examiner, Guangzu was appointed palace attendant censor and submitted the first memorial on orthodox versus heterodox learning.

sentences.zh: 及奏名，光祖被旨入院拆號，與澹席甫逼，澹曰：「近日風采一新。」

translations.literal: When the names were announced, Guangzu was ordered into the academy to open the rolls; he and Dan sat close; Dan said: 'Your bearing of late is quite renewed.
translations.idiomatic: When the examination results were announced, Guangzu was ordered into the academy to open the rolls. Seated beside Dan, he heard Dan say, "Your spirit has been quite renewed of late.

sentences.zh: 光祖曰：「非立異也，但嘗為大諫言者，今日言之耳。」

translations.literal: Guangzu said: 'It is not to stand apart; only as one who once spoke as chief remonstrator, I speak today—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu replied, "I am not trying to be contrary. I am only saying today what I once said as chief remonstrator."

sentences.zh: 既出，同院謂光祖曰：「何自然見君所上章，數夕恍惚，餌定志丸，他可知也。」

translations.literal: After leaving, a colleague in the academy said to Guangzu: 'When He Ziran saw the memorial you submitted, for several nights he was distraught and took calming pills—the rest can be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward a colleague told Guangzu, "When He Ziran read your memorial he was unsettled for days and took calming pills. You can guess the rest.

sentences.zh: 進御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 澹有本生繼母喪，乞有司定所服，禮寺言當解官，澹引不逮事之文，乞下給、諫議之。

translations.literal: Dan had mourning for a birth mother who was a stepmother; he asked the authorities to fix his mourning garment; the Ritual Office said he should leave office; Dan cited the text on not reaching full mourning and asked that it be sent to drafting and remonstrance officials for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan's birth mother, who had been his stepmother, died, he asked the authorities to determine his mourning obligations. The Ritual Office ruled he should leave office, but Dan cited provisions on incomplete mourning and asked the drafting and remonstrance officers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 太學生喬嚞、朱有成等移書於澹，謂：「足下自長臺諫，此綱常之所係也。

translations.literal: Imperial Academy students Qiao Xi, Zhu Youcheng, and others sent a letter to Dan saying: 'You yourself head the remonstrance bureau—this bears on the constants of the bonds.
translations.idiomatic: Academy students Qiao Xi, Zhu Youcheng, and others wrote to Dan: "As head of the censorate, you bear responsibility for the moral order of the realm.

sentences.zh: 四十餘年以所生繼母事之，及其終也，反以為生不逮而不持心喪，可乎？

translations.literal: For more than forty years you served the birth mother who was stepmother; at her end you instead take that birth did not reach full mourning and will not observe heart-mourning—can this be right?
translations.idiomatic: For more than forty years you treated your birth mother as your stepmother served her. Now at her death you claim the bond did not reach full mourning and refuse heart-mourning. Can this be right?

sentences.zh: 奉常，禮所由出，顧以臺諫、給舍議之，識者有以窺之矣。」

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices is where ritual issues forth—yet you would have censors and drafting officials discuss it; the discerning can see through this.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices is the source of ritual law, yet you would have censors and drafting officers debate it instead. Perceptive observers can see your motive."

sentences.zh: 澹乃去。

translations.literal: Dan thereupon left office.
translations.idiomatic: Dan thereupon resigned.

sentences.zh: 終制，除煥章閣學士、知泉州，移明州。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Academician of the Hall for Glorifying Culture and prefect of Quanzhou, then transferred to Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was appointed academician of the Hall for Glorifying Culture and prefect of Quanzhou, later transferred to Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，朱熹、彭龜年以論韓侂胄俱絀，澹還為中丞，怨趙汝愚不援引。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong ascended, Zhu Xi and Peng Guinian were both demoted for criticizing Han Tuozhou; Dan returned as censor-in-chief, resenting Zhao Ruyu for not recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong ascended the throne, Zhu Xi and Peng Guinian were demoted for criticizing Han Tuozhou. Dan returned as censor-in-chief, resentful that Zhao Ruyu had not promoted him.

sentences.zh: 汝愚時已免相，復詆其廢壞壽皇良法美意，汝愚落職罷祠。

translations.literal: Ruyu had already been removed as chief councilor; Dan again slandered him for abolishing the good laws and fine intentions of Emperor Shouhuang; Ruyu was stripped of office and dismissed from his sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu had already left the chief ministership. Dan attacked him again for overturning Shouhuang's good policies, and Ruyu was stripped of rank and dismissed from his sinecure.

sentences.zh: 又言：「專門之學，流而為偽。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Specialized learning flows and becomes false.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Specialized schools of thought degenerate into false learning.

sentences.zh: 願風厲學者，專師孔、孟，不得自相標榜。」

translations.literal: I wish to admonish scholars sternly to take Confucius and Mencius alone as masters and not to label themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that scholars be exhorted to follow Confucius and Mencius alone and not to proclaim factions among themselves."

sentences.zh: 除同知樞密院事、參知政事，遷知樞密院。

translations.literal: He was appointed Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Participant in Governance, then promoted to Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate commissioner of military affairs and participant in governance, then promoted to commissioner.

sentences.zh: 吳曦賄通時宰，規圖帥蜀，未及賄澹，韓侂胄已許之，澹持不可。

translations.literal: Wu Xi bribed the chief ministers of the time and plotted to command Shu; before he could bribe Dan, Han Tuozhou had already agreed; Dan held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi bribed the chief ministers to secure command of Shu. Before he could bribe Dan, Han Tuozhou had already promised him the post. Dan objected.

sentences.zh: 侂胄怒曰：「始以君肯相就，黜偽學，汲引至此，今顧立異耶？」

translations.literal: Tuozhou angrily said: 'At first I thought you willing to join me, banishing false learning and drawing you up to this—now you turn contrary?
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou raged, "I brought you in because you would banish false learning and serve my cause. Now you turn against me?"

sentences.zh: 以資政殿大學士提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and charged with the Palace of the Cavernous Sky.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and put in charge of the Palace of the Cavernous Sky.

sentences.zh: 起知福州。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled to serve as prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 澹居外，常怏怏失意，以書祈侂胄，有曰：「跡雖東冶，心在南園。」

translations.literal: Living outside the capital Dan was often discontent and wrote to Tuozhou pleading, saying: 'My tracks may be in the eastern administration, but my heart is in the Southern Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Exiled from court, Dan was often discontent and wrote to Tuozhou, saying, "Though my body is in the east, my heart remains in the Southern Garden."

sentences.zh: 南園，侂胄家圃也。

translations.literal: The Southern Garden was Tuozhou's family estate.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Garden was Tuozhou's private estate.

sentences.zh: 侂胄憐之。

translations.literal: Tuozhou pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou took pity on him.

sentences.zh: 進觀文殿學士，尋移知隆興府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and soon transferred as prefect of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and soon transferred to Longxing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後除江淮制置大使兼知建康府，移使湖北，兼知江陵。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Commissioner for the Huai and Jiang circuits and concurrent prefect of Jiankang, then transferred as commissioner for Hubei and concurrent prefect of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed commissioner for the Huai and Jiang circuits with concurrent charge of Jiankang, then transferred to Hubei with concurrent charge of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 奉祠卒，贈少師。

translations.literal: He died while holding a sinecure and was posthumously given the title Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died while holding a sinecure post and was posthumously ennobled as junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 澹美姿容，善談論，少年取科名，急於榮進，阿附權姦，斥逐善類，主偽黨之禁，賢士為之一空。

translations.literal: Dan had handsome features and was skilled in discourse; in youth he took the examination degree and was eager for advancement; he fawned on powerful villains, drove out the good, presided over the ban on the false faction, and worthy men were emptied out.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and eloquent, Dan won his degree young and hungered for advancement. He curried favor with powerful villains, drove out the worthy, enforced the ban on false learning, and left the ranks of talent nearly bare.

sentences.zh: 其後更化，凶黨俱逐，澹以早退倖免，優遊散地幾二十年。

translations.literal: Afterward when policy changed, the vicious faction was all driven out; Dan, by early retirement, luckily escaped and idled in minor posts for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When policy later changed and the vicious faction was expelled, Dan escaped punishment through early retirement and lived at ease in minor posts for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 時金人請和，約為叔侄之國，且以歸疆為請。

translations.literal: At the time the Jurchens sought peace, proposing a state of uncle and nephew, and also asked for the return of territory.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Jurchens sought peace on terms that Song accept uncle-nephew status and return territory to them.

sentences.zh: 栗上封事言：

translations.literal: Li submitted a sealed memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Li submitted a sealed memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 「前日之和，誠為非計。

translations.literal: The peace of former days was truly an unwise plan.
translations.idiomatic: "The peace concluded before was indeed a mistake.

sentences.zh: 然徽宗梓宮、慈寧行殿在彼，為是而屈，猶有名焉。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Huizong's coffin palace and the Cining traveling hall were there; to yield for this still had a name.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huizong's coffin and the Cining traveling hall remained in their hands; to yield for that still had some justification.

sentences.zh: 今日之和，臣不知其說也。

translations.literal: Today's peace—I do not know its rationale.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot see the rationale for peace today.

sentences.zh: 宗廟之仇，而事之以弟侄，其忍使祖宗聞之乎！

translations.literal: An enemy of the ancestral temple, yet treating them as nephew—can we bear to let the ancestors hear of this!
translations.idiomatic: They are enemies of our ancestral temple, yet we would treat them as uncle and nephew. Can we bear for our ancestors to hear of this?

sentences.zh: 無唐、鄧，則荊、襄有齒寒之憂；

translations.literal: Without Tang and Deng, Jing and Xiang would have the worry of cold teeth;
translations.idiomatic: Without Tang and Deng, Jing and Xiang would face the danger of a broken barrier;

sentences.zh: 無泗、海，則淮東之備達于真、楊，海道之防遍於明、越矣。

translations.literal: without Si and Hai, Huaidong defenses would reach Zhen and Yang, and coastal defenses would spread through Ming and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: without Si and Hai, defenses east of the Huai would extend to Zhen and Yang, and coastal defenses would stretch from Ming to Yue.

sentences.zh: 議者皆言和戎之幣少，養兵之費多，不知講和之後，朝廷能不養兵乎？

translations.literal: Advocates all say peace tribute is little and maintaining troops costly; they do not know that after making peace, can the court fail to maintain troops?
translations.idiomatic: Advocates say peace payments cost less than maintaining armies, but do they imagine the court will stop maintaining troops after a treaty?

sentences.zh: 今東南民力，陛下之所知也，朝廷安得而不較乎？

translations.literal: The people's strength in the southeast—Your Majesty knows it; how can the court fail to reckon with it?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty knows the strain on the southeast. How can the court ignore it?

sentences.zh: 且非徒無益而已。

translations.literal: Moreover it is not merely without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: And it is not merely useless.

sentences.zh: 與之歲幣，是畏之矣。

translations.literal: Giving them annual tribute is to fear them.
translations.idiomatic: Paying annual tribute means fearing them.

sentences.zh: 三軍之情，安得不懈弛；

translations.literal: The spirit of the three armies—how can it not slacken;
translations.idiomatic: Army morale will inevitably slacken;

sentences.zh: 歸正之心，安得不攜貳。

translations.literal: the hearts of those who returned to the fold—how can they not waver.
translations.idiomatic: and the loyalty of those who defected to us will inevitably waver.

sentences.zh: 為今日計，宜停使勿遣，遷延其期。

translations.literal: For today's plan, envoys should be stopped and not sent; the term should be postponed.
translations.idiomatic: For the present, envoys should be halted and the deadline postponed.

sentences.zh: 比至來春，別無動息，徐於境上移書，諭以兩國誓言。

translations.literal: By next spring, if there is no other movement, slowly at the border send a letter expounding the two states' sworn words.
translations.idiomatic: By next spring, if nothing changes, we can slowly send word across the border invoking the two states' sworn oaths.

sentences.zh: 敗之自彼，信不由衷，雖盟無益。

translations.literal: If defeat comes from them, faith not from the heart—even with alliance there is no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If they break faith, no alliance will help.

sentences.zh: 自今宜守分界，休息生靈，不煩聘使之往來，各保疆場之無事，焉用疲弊州縣，以奉犬羊之使乎？」

translations.literal: From now we should guard the boundary, rest the people, not trouble envoys coming and going, each keep the borders without incident—why weary and impoverish prefectures and counties to serve the envoys of dogs and sheep?
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth we should hold the border, let the people rest, and cease sending envoys back and forth. Let each side keep its territory in peace. Why exhaust our prefectures and counties to entertain the envoys of barbarians?"

sentences.zh: 孝宗懲創紹興權臣之弊，躬攬權綱，不以責任臣下，栗言：「人主蒞權，大臣審權，爭臣議權，王侯、貴戚善撓權者也，左右近習善竊權者也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong, chastened by the abuses of powerful ministers in Shaoxing, personally grasped the reins of power and did not entrust responsibility to ministers; Li said: 'The ruler presides over power, great ministers examine power, remonstrators debate power; kings, marquises, and noble kin are skilled at disturbing power; attendants close at hand are skilled at stealing power.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong, chastened by Shaoxing's powerful ministers, personally held the reins and did not delegate authority. Li wrote: "The ruler presides over power, ministers examine it, and remonstrators debate it. Princes and noble kin are adept at disturbing it; close attendants are adept at stealing it.

sentences.zh: 權在大臣，則大臣重；

translations.literal: When power is with great ministers, great ministers are weighty;
translations.idiomatic: When power rests with ministers, ministers grow weighty;

sentences.zh: 權在邇臣，則邇臣重；

translations.literal: when power is with near ministers, near ministers are weighty;
translations.idiomatic: when it rests with lesser ministers, they grow weighty;

sentences.zh: 權在爭臣，則爭臣重。

translations.literal: when power is with remonstrators, remonstrators are weighty.
translations.idiomatic: when it rests with remonstrators, remonstrators grow weighty.

sentences.zh: 是故人主常患權在臣下，必欲收攬而獨持之，然未有能獨持之者也。

translations.literal: Therefore rulers constantly fear power in subordinates and must wish to gather it in and hold it alone—yet none has been able to hold it alone.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers therefore constantly fear power in their subordinates and try to gather it all to themselves, yet none has ever truly held it alone.

sentences.zh: 不使大臣持之，則王侯、貴戚得而持之矣；

translations.literal: If great ministers are not allowed to hold it, then kings, marquises, and noble kin obtain and hold it;
translations.idiomatic: If ministers are not allowed to hold power, princes and noble kin will seize it;

sentences.zh: 不使邇臣審之，爭臣議之，則左右近習得而議之矣。

translations.literal: if near ministers are not allowed to examine it and remonstrators debate it, then attendants close at hand obtain and debate it.
translations.idiomatic: if lesser ministers do not examine it and remonstrators do not debate it, close attendants will take it over.

sentences.zh: 人主顧謂得其權而自執之，豈不誤哉。

translations.literal: The ruler supposes he has obtained power and holds it himself—is this not mistaken?
translations.idiomatic: For the ruler to imagine he has seized power and holds it himself—is this not a delusion?

sentences.zh: 是故明主使人持權而不以權與之，收攬其權而不肯獨持之。」

translations.literal: Therefore the enlightened ruler makes others hold power without giving power to them, gathers power in without being willing to hold it alone.
translations.idiomatic: The enlightened ruler therefore lets others wield power without surrendering it to them, and gathers authority in without insisting on holding it alone."

sentences.zh: 至有「以鹿為馬、以雞為鸞」之語。

translations.literal: He even had the words 'calling a deer a horse, calling a chicken a phoenix.'
translations.idiomatic: He even wrote of "calling a deer a horse and a chicken a phoenix."

sentences.zh: 方奉對時，讀至「人主常患權在臣下，必欲收攬而獨持之」，孝宗稱善，栗徐曰：「臣意尚在下文。」

translations.literal: While presenting his response, when he read to 'rulers constantly fear power in subordinates and must wish to gather it in and hold it alone,' Xiaozong praised it; Li slowly said: 'My meaning is still in what follows.
translations.idiomatic: While presenting his memorial, when he reached the passage on rulers fearing power in subordinates, Xiaozong praised it. Li said slowly, "Your Majesty, my point lies in what follows.

sentences.zh: 執政有訴于孝宗曰：「林栗謂臣等指鹿為馬，臣實不願與之同朝。」

translations.literal: A chief minister complained to Xiaozong: 'Lin Li says we ministers call deer horses—I truly do not wish to share court with him.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister complained to Xiaozong, "Lin Li accuses us of calling deer horses. I cannot serve in the same court with him.

sentences.zh: 乃出知江州。

translations.literal: He was thereupon sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li was accordingly sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 有旨省併江州屯駐一軍，栗奏：「辛巳、甲申，金再犯兩淮，賴江州一軍分佈防托，故舒、蘄、黃三州獨不被寇。

translations.literal: An edict ordered merging and reducing one army garrisoned at Jiangzhou. Li memorialized: 'In xinsi and jiashen the Jin again invaded the two Huai circuits; thanks to one Jiangzhou army distributed for defense, the three prefectures Shu, Qi, and Huang alone were not raided.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proposed consolidating the army stationed at Jiangzhou. Li memorialized: "When the Jin invaded the two Huai circuits in 1161 and 1164, it was the Jiangzhou garrison that held the line, so Shu, Qi, and Huang alone escaped attack.

sentences.zh: 本州上至鄂渚七百里，下至池陽五百里；

translations.literal: From this prefecture it is seven hundred li up to Ezhu and five hundred li down to Chiyang;
translations.idiomatic: From Jiangzhou it is seven hundred li upstream to Ezhou and five hundred li downstream to Chizhou;

sentences.zh: 平時屯戍，誠若無益，萬一有警，鄂渚之戍，上越荊、襄，池陽之師，下流增備，中間千里藩籬，誠為虛闕。

translations.literal: in normal times the garrison seems truly useless, but if there is an alarm, the garrison at Ezhu crosses Jing and Xiang above, the force at Chiyang augments defenses below, and the thousand-li barrier in between would truly be left void.
translations.idiomatic: in peacetime the garrison may seem useless, but in an emergency troops at Ezhou would cover Jing and Xiang upstream while forces at Chizhou reinforced the lower reaches, leaving a thousand-li gap in between.

sentences.zh: 無以一夫之議，而廢長江千里之防。」

translations.literal: One must not, on one man's opinion, abolish defense along a thousand li of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: We must not abolish a thousand li of Yangzi defense on one man's say-so."

sentences.zh: 由是軍得無動。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army was left unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: The army was therefore left in place.

sentences.zh: 以吏部員外郎召。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 冬至，有事南郊，前期十日，百執事聽誓戒；

translations.literal: At the winter solstice there was to be sacrifice at the Southern Suburb; ten days beforehand the hundred officials heard the oath of abstinence;
translations.idiomatic: For the winter solstice sacrifice at the Southern Suburb, ten days in advance all officials took the abstinence oath;

sentences.zh: 會廢節，有旨上壽不用樂，迨宴金使，乃有權用樂之命。

translations.literal: it happened that a festival was abolished, and an edict said birthday felicitations should use no music; yet when entertaining Jin envoys there was a provisional order allowing music.
translations.idiomatic: a festival had been cancelled and an edict forbade music for birthday felicitations, yet when entertaining Jin envoys a provisional order allowed music.

sentences.zh: 栗以為不可，致書宰相，不聽，乃乞免充舉冊官，以狀申朝廷曰：「若聽樂則廢齋，廢齋則不敢以祭。

translations.literal: Li held this impossible, wrote to the chief councilor, was not heeded, and begged to be excused from serving as ritual officer, submitting to the court: 'If music is heard, fasting is broken; if fasting is broken I dare not sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Li objected, wrote the chief councilor, was ignored, and asked to be excused from the ritual commission, telling the court: "If music is played, fasting is void; if fasting is void I dare not sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 祖宗二百年事天之禮，今因一介行人而廢之。

translations.literal: The two hundred years of our ancestors' ritual of serving Heaven is now abandoned for one foreign envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred years of our ancestors' rites to Heaven would be abandoned for one foreign envoy.

sentences.zh: 天之可畏，過於外夷遠矣。」

translations.literal: Heaven is to be feared more than distant barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is more to be feared than distant barbarians."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 兼皇子慶王府直講，有旨令二王非時招延講讀官，相與議論時政，期盡規益。

translations.literal: Concurrently Lecturer at the Princely Mansion of Prince Qing, an edict ordered the two princes to summon lecturing officials at irregular times to discuss current affairs, hoping for full remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: As concurrent lecturer at Prince Qing's mansion, an edict ordered the two princes to summon lecturers at will to discuss current affairs.

sentences.zh: 栗以為不可，疏言：「漢武帝為戾太子開博望苑，卒敗太子；

translations.literal: Li held this impossible and memorialized: 'Emperor Wu of Han opened Bowang Park for Crown Prince Li and in the end ruined the prince;
translations.idiomatic: Li objected, writing: "Emperor Wu opened Bowang Park for Crown Prince Li and ruined him;

sentences.zh: 唐太宗為魏王泰立文學館，卒敗魏王。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang established a Literary Hall for Prince Tai and in the end ruined Prince Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong established a Literary Hall for Prince Tai and ruined him.

sentences.zh: 古者教世子與吾祖宗之所以輔導太子、諸王，惟以講經讀史為事，他無預焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity teaching the heir and how our ancestors guided crown princes and princes used only lecturing on classics and reading history; nothing else was involved.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient teaching of heirs and our ancestors' guidance of princes rested on classics and history alone.

sentences.zh: 若使議論時政，則是對子議父，古人謂之無禮，不可不留聖意。」

translations.literal: If they are made to discuss current affairs, it is the son discussing the father—what ancients called lack of ritual. This must remain in the sage mind.'
translations.idiomatic: To discuss current affairs is for sons to debate fathers—what ancients called impiety. Your Majesty must take note."

sentences.zh: 除右司員外郎，遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Right Office and transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the right office and transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 太廟祫享之制，始祖東向，昭南向，穆北向，別廟神主祔于祖姑之下，隨本室南北向而無西向之位。

translations.literal: For the collective sacrifice in the Grand Temple, the founding ancestor faced east, zhao south, mu north; spirits of separate temples were attached below the founding ancestress, following the main chamber north and south without a west-facing position.
translations.idiomatic: In collective Grand Temple sacrifice, the founder faced east, zhao south, mu north; separate-temple tablets were placed below the founding ancestress without west-facing positions.

sentences.zh: 紹興、乾道間，懿節、安穆二后升祔，有司設幄西向。

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing and Qiandao eras Empresses Yijie and Anmu were elevated to attachment; the officials set canopies facing west.
translations.idiomatic: When Empresses Yijie and Anmu were enshrined in Shaoxing and Qiandao, officials set west-facing canopies.

sentences.zh: 逮安恭皇后新祔，有司承前失，其西向之位，幾與僖祖相對。

translations.literal: When the new Empress Angong was attached, officials followed the earlier error; the west-facing position nearly faced the founder Xizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Angong was newly enshrined, officials repeated the error until the west-facing position nearly faced Founder Xizu.

sentences.zh: 栗辨正之。

translations.literal: Li corrected this.
translations.idiomatic: Li corrected it.

sentences.zh: 除直寶文閣、知湖州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed direct academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 栗朝辭曰：

translations.literal: At court leave Li said:
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience Li said:

sentences.zh: 「臣聞漢人賈誼號通達國體，其所上書至於痛哭流涕者，考其指歸，大抵以一身諭天下之勢。

translations.literal: 'I have heard the Han man Jia Yi was called penetrating in national principle; in his memorials he even reached weeping and shedding tears; examining his aim, it was mostly to liken the whole realm's condition to one body.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Jia Yi, called penetrating in statecraft, wept in his memorials because he likened the realm's condition to a single body.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：『天下之勢方病大瘇。

translations.literal: He said: 'The realm's condition is like a great swelling.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: 'The realm's condition is like a great swelling.

sentences.zh: 非徒瘇也，又苦𨁣盭。

translations.literal: It is not merely swelling; it also suffers from crippling lameness.
translations.idiomatic: It is not merely swollen; it also suffers crippling lameness.

sentences.zh: 又類辟，且病痱。』

translations.literal: It is also like epilepsy, and moreover suffers from numbness.'
translations.idiomatic: It is also like epilepsy, and suffers numbness.'

sentences.zh: 臣每見士大夫好論時事，臣輒舉以問之：『今日國體，於四百四病之中，名為何病？

translations.literal: Whenever I see gentlemen fond of discussing current affairs I cite this and ask: 'Of the four hundred and four diseases, what is today's national condition named?
translations.idiomatic: When gentlemen discuss current affairs I ask: 'Of four hundred and four diseases, what is ours called?

sentences.zh: 能言其病者猶未必能處其方，不能言其病而輒處其方，其誤人之死，必矣。』

translations.literal: Those who can name the disease may not yet treat it; those who cannot name the disease yet prescribe— they surely kill men.
translations.idiomatic: Those who can name the disease may not cure it; those who prescribe without naming it surely kill.

sentences.zh: 聞臣之言者不忿則默，間有反以詰臣，即對之曰：『今日之病，名為風虛，其狀半身不隨是也。

translations.literal: Those who hear me are not angry but silent; occasionally some turn and question me, and I answer: 'Today's disease is called wind with vacuity; its sign is half the body not following—that is it.
translations.idiomatic: Hearers grow silent; if challenged I answer: 'Today's disease is wind with inner vacuity—half the body does not obey.

sentences.zh: 風者在外，虛者在內，真氣內耗，故風邪自外而乘之，忽中于人，應時僵仆，則靖康之變是也。

translations.literal: Wind is outside, vacuity inside; true qi is depleted within, so wind evil rides in from without and suddenly strikes a man, stiff and falling—that was the Jingkang disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wind is external, vacuity internal; when true qi fails, wind strikes from without—as at Jingkang.

sentences.zh: 幸而元氣猶存，故仆而復起，則建炎之興是也。

translations.literal: Fortunately primal qi still remained, so after falling one rose again—that was the Jianyan revival.
translations.idiomatic: Primal qi remained, so after falling the realm rose again—as at Jianyan.

sentences.zh: 然元氣雖存，邪氣尚盛，自淮以北皆吾故壤，而號令不能及，正朔不能加，有異於半身不隨者乎？

translations.literal: Yet though primal qi remained, evil qi was still strong; north of the Huai all is our old soil, yet orders cannot reach it, the calendar cannot be imposed—is this not like half the body not following?
translations.idiomatic: Yet evil qi remained strong; north of the Huai is our old soil, yet we cannot rule it—is this not half a body paralyzed?

sentences.zh: 非但半身不隨而已，半身存者，凜凜乎畏風邪之乘而不能以自安也。』

translations.literal: It is not merely half not following; the half that remains trembles in fear of wind evil and cannot rest secure.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, the surviving half lives in fear of wind and cannot rest.

sentences.zh: 今日論者，譬如痿人之不忘起，奚必賢智之士，然後與國同其願哉？

translations.literal: Today's debaters are like paralytics who cannot forget rising; must one be wise to share the state's wish?
translations.idiomatic: Today's debaters are paralytics who forget they cannot rise; need one be wise to share the state's wish?

sentences.zh: 而市道庸流，口傳耳受，苟欲嘗試以售其方，則蕩熨針石，雜然並進，非體虛之人所宜輕受也。

translations.literal: Market peddlers hear by mouth and try their prescriptions—steaming, ironing, needles, and stones all rush in; this is not what a vacuous body should lightly receive.
translations.idiomatic: Peddlers hear rumors and rush in remedies—steaming, needles, stones—not for a vacuous body.

sentences.zh: 聞之醫曰：『中風偏廢，年五十以下而氣盛者易治。

translations.literal: Physicians say: 'In wind paralysis, those under fifty with strong qi are easy to cure.
translations.idiomatic: Physicians say: 'In wind paralysis, the young with strong qi are curable.

sentences.zh: 蓋真氣與邪氣相敵，真氣盛則邪氣衰，真氣行則邪氣去。

translations.literal: True qi contends with evil; when true qi is strong evil weakens; when true qi moves evil departs.
translations.idiomatic: When true qi meets evil, strength drives evil out.

sentences.zh: 然真氣不充滿於半存之身，則無以及偏廢之體。

translations.literal: Yet true qi must fill the half that survives before it can reach the paralyzed half.
translations.idiomatic: True qi must fill the surviving half before reaching the paralyzed part.

sentences.zh: 故欲起此疾者，必禁其嗜欲，節其思慮，愛其氣血，養其精神，使半存之身，日以充實，則陽氣周流，脈絡宜暢，將不覺舍杖而行。

translations.literal: Therefore to rouse this illness one must forbid appetites, limit thought, cherish qi and blood, nourish spirit, so the surviving half daily grows full; then yang circulates, channels open, and one will set aside the staff and walk without noticing.
translations.idiomatic: One must curb appetites, limit thought, nourish qi and spirit until the surviving half strengthens and yang flows again.

sentences.zh: 若急於愈疾而不顧其本，百毒入口，五臟受風，風邪之盛未可卒去，而真氣之存者日以耗亡，故中風再至者多不能救。』

translations.literal: If one hurries cure without regard to the root, poisons enter, the five viscera take wind, wind evil cannot soon depart and true qi daily wastes—most who suffer wind twice cannot be saved.'
translations.idiomatic: Hurry cure without rooting and poisons enter; true qi wastes away and a second stroke kills.

sentences.zh: 臣愚有感於斯言，竊謂賈誼復生，為陛下言，無以易此。」

translations.literal: I am moved by this and think if Jia Yi were reborn to speak to Your Majesty, he could not improve on it.'
translations.idiomatic: If Jia Yi were reborn he could not improve on this.'

sentences.zh: 知興化軍，又移南劍，除夔路提點刑獄，改知夔州，加直敷文閣。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Xinghua, transferred to Nanjian, was appointed Judicial Intendant of Kuizhou circuit, then prefect of Kuizhou, and given the added title Direct Academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Xinghua and Nanjian, became judicial intendant and prefect of Kuizhou, with the added title direct academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture.

sentences.zh: 夔屬郡曰施州，其羈縻郡曰思州。

translations.literal: A subordinate prefecture of Kuizhou was Shizhou; its attached prefecture was Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kuizhou's subordinate Shizhou had the attached Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 施民譚汝翼者，與知思州田汝弼交惡，會汝弼卒，汝翼帥兵二千人伐其喪。

translations.literal: A Shizhou man Tan Ruyi feuded with Sizhou prefect Tian Rubi; when Rubi died Ruyi led two thousand men to attack the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Ruyi of Shizhou feuded with Tian Rubi of Sizhou; when Rubi died Ruyi attacked the funeral with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 汝弼之子祖周深入報復，兵交於三州之境，施、黔大震。

translations.literal: Rubi's son Zuzhou struck deep in revenge; armies clashed across three prefectures; Shizhou and Qian were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi's son Zuzhou counterattacked; fighting spread across three prefectures.

sentences.zh: 汝翼復繕甲兵，料丁壯，以重幣借兵諸洞，而乞師于帥府。

translations.literal: Ruyi again repaired arms, mustered able men, borrowed troops from caves with heavy bribes, and begged forces from the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyi rearmed, mustered men, borrowed tribal troops, and begged aid from headquarters.

sentences.zh: 栗曰：「汝翼實召亂者。」

translations.literal: Li said: 'Ruyi truly summoned disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: Li said: 'Ruyi truly provoked this disorder.'

sentences.zh: 移檄罷兵，乃選屬吏往攝兵職，以漸收汝翼之權。

translations.literal: He moved a proclamation to halt troops, chose subordinate officials to take military duties, and gradually recovered Ruyi's power.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered troops halted, sent subordinates to take command, and gradually stripped Ruyi's power.

sentences.zh: 命兵馬鈐轄按閱諸州，密檄至施，就攝州事。

translations.literal: He ordered the military controller to inspect the prefectures and secretly sent a dispatch to Shizhou to take charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the military controller to inspect prefectures and secretly sent orders to Shizhou to assume charge.

sentences.zh: 汝翼不之覺，已乃皇遽遁入成都。

translations.literal: Ruyi did not notice; only then did he flee in panic into Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyi noticed too late and fled to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 事聞，孝宗親劄賜栗及成都制置使陳峴曰：「田氏猶是羈縻州郡，譚氏乃夔路豪族，又且首為釁端，帥閫不能彈壓，縱其至此。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Xiaozong personally wrote to Li and Chengdu commissioner Chen Xian: 'The Tian clan is still an attached prefecture; the Tan clan is a great house of Kuizhou and moreover first made trouble; the commander could not suppress them and let it reach this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong wrote Li and commissioner Chen Xian: 'The Tians are attached tribes; the Tans are Kuizhou magnates who started the trouble; the commander failed to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 如尚不悛，未免加兵，除其元惡。」

translations.literal: If they still do not repent, troops cannot be avoided to eliminate the chief villains.'
translations.idiomatic: If they do not repent, troops must eliminate the ringleaders.'

sentences.zh: 時汝翼在成都，聞之逃歸，調集家丁及役八砦義軍，列陳於沱河橋與官軍戰，潰，汝翼遁去，俘其徒四十有三人，獲甲鎧器仗三萬一千。

translations.literal: At the time Ruyi was in Chengdu; hearing this he fled back, gathered household retainers and eight-fortress militia, arrayed battle at the Tuo River bridge against government troops, was routed and fled; forty-three followers were captured with thirty-one thousand suits of armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyi fled Chengdu, rallied retainers and militia, fought at Tuo River bridge, was routed; forty-three were captured with vast arms.

sentences.zh: 栗取其巨惡者九人誅之。

translations.literal: Li executed nine of the greatest villains.
translations.idiomatic: Li executed nine chief culprits.

sentences.zh: 田祖周由是懼，與其母冉氏謀獻黔江田業，計錢九十萬緡以贖罪，蠻徼遂安。

translations.literal: Tian Zuzhou thereupon feared; with his mother Ran he plotted to offer Qianjiang fields worth nine hundred thousand strings to redeem guilt, and the frontier was then quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Zuzhou, fearing execution, offered fields worth nine hundred thousand strings; the frontier quieted.

sentences.zh: 既而汝翼入都訴栗受田氏金，詔以汝翼屬吏，省劄下夔州。

translations.literal: Later Ruyi entered the capital to accuse Li of taking Tian gold; an edict handed Ruyi to officials and sent a provincial dispatch to Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyi later accused Li of taking Tian bribes; an edict sent him to officials in Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 栗親書奏狀繳還，並辨其事。

translations.literal: Li personally wrote a memorial returning it and clarifying the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Li returned the dispatch with a clarifying memorial.

sentences.zh: 上大怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 會近臣有救解者，尋坐栗身為帥臣，擅格上命，鐫職罷歸。

translations.literal: When a close attendant interceded, Li was soon punished as a frontier commander who on his own blocked imperial orders, was demoted and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: After intercession, Li was punished for blocking imperial orders and sent home.

sentences.zh: 既而理寺追究，事白，貸汝翼死，幽置紹興府。

translations.literal: Soon the judicial office investigated and the matter was cleared; Ruyi's death was commuted and he was confined in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation cleared Li; Ruyi's death sentence was commuted to confinement in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 居頃之，詔栗累更事任，清介有聞，復直寶文閣、廣南西路轉運判官，就改提點刑獄，又改知潭州。

translations.literal: Before long an edict said Li had served repeatedly with a reputation for integrity, restored him as Direct Academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and transport judge of Guangnan West, then judicial intendant, then prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li was restored for integrity to academician and posts in Guangnan West and Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 除秘閣修撰，進集英殿修撰、知隆興府。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler of the Privy Archive, advanced to Compiler of the Hall for Assembled Eminence and prefect of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: He became privy archive compiler, then compiler of the Hall for Assembled Eminence and prefect of Longxing.

sentences.zh: 召對便殿，奏乞仿唐制置補闕、拾遺左右各一員，不以糾彈為責。

translations.literal: Summoned to the informal hall he memorialized to follow Tang in establishing one remonstrance and one supplementation officer on left and right, not charged with impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court he asked to restore Tang-style remonstrance and supplementation officers not charged with impeachment.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 除兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 朱熹以江西提刑召為兵部郎官，熹既入國門，未就職。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi, as Jiangxi judicial intendant, was summoned as Lang official in the Ministry of War; Xi entered the capital gate but had not taken office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi was summoned from Jiangxi as war ministry lang official but had not taken office.

sentences.zh: 栗與熹相見，論《易》與《西銘》不合。

translations.literal: Li met Xi and discussed the Book of Changes and Western Inscription without agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Li met Xi and disputed the Book of Changes and Western Inscription.

sentences.zh: 至是，栗遣吏部趣之，熹以腳疾請告。

translations.literal: At this Li sent the Ministry to urge him; Xi pleaded foot ailment and asked leave.
translations.idiomatic: Li sent the ministry to hurry him; Xi pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 栗遂論：「熹本無學術，徒竊張載、程頤之緒餘，為浮誕宗主，謂之道學，妄自推尊。

translations.literal: Li then argued: 'Xi originally had no learning; he merely stole the leavings of Zhang Zai and Cheng Yi, made a floating absurd sect, called it the Way-learning, and presumptuously exalted himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li attacked Xi: 'He has no learning, only scraps of Zhang and Cheng; he calls it Way-learning and exalts himself.

sentences.zh: 所至輒攜門生十數人，習為春秋、戰國之態，妄希孔、孟歷聘之風，繩以治世之法，則亂人之首也。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he carried a dozen disciples practicing Spring and Autumn and Warring States manner, vainly hoping for Confucius and Mencius' touring style; measured by law for governing the age, he is chief of disorderers.
translations.idiomatic: He tours with disciples aping ancient sages; by standards of governance he is a chief disorderer.

sentences.zh: 今采其虛名，俾之入奏，將置朝列，以次收用。

translations.literal: Now his empty fame is taken to bring him to court for gradual employment.
translations.idiomatic: Now his empty fame brings him to court for appointment.

sentences.zh: 而熹聞命之初，遷延道途，邀索高價，門生迭為遊說，政府許以風聞，然後入門。

translations.literal: When he first received the order he delayed on the road, demanded high price; disciples lobbied in turn; the government allowed rumor—only then did he enter.
translations.idiomatic: He delayed on the road, demanded high price, and let disciples lobby before entering.

sentences.zh: 既經陛對，得旨除郎，而輒懷不滿，傲睨累日，不肯供職，是豈張載、程頤之學教之然也？

translations.literal: After audience he received appointment as lang yet was discontent, looked down arrogantly for days and would not serve—is this what Zhang and Cheng's learning teaches?
translations.idiomatic: Given a lang post he was discontent, refused duty for days—is this Zhang and Cheng's teaching?

sentences.zh: 緣熹既除兵部郎官，在臣合有統攝，若不舉劾，厥罪惟均。

translations.literal: Since Xi was appointed war lang and falls under my supervision, if I do not impeach the fault is equally mine.
translations.idiomatic: As his supervisor I must impeach or share the fault.

sentences.zh: 望將熹停罷，姑令循省，以為事君無禮者之戒。」

translations.literal: I hope Xi will be suspended for reflection, as a warning to those disrespectful to the ruler.'
translations.idiomatic: Suspend Xi for reflection as a warning to the disrespectful.'

sentences.zh: 上謂其言過當，而大臣畏栗之強，莫敢深論。

translations.literal: The emperor said his words were excessive, yet great ministers feared Li's force and dared not debate deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said he went too far, but ministers feared Li and did not debate.

sentences.zh: 太常博士葉適獨上封事辯之曰：

translations.literal: Only Court Doctor Ye Shi alone submitted a sealed memorial in rebuttal:
translations.idiomatic: Only Ye Shi submitted a sealed rebuttal:

sentences.zh: 「考栗之辭，始末參驗，無一實者。

translations.literal: 'Examining Li's words start to finish, not one is real.
translations.idiomatic: 'Examining Li's words, not one is real.

sentences.zh: 其中『謂之道學』一語，無實最甚。

translations.literal: Among them the phrase "called Way-learning" is least real.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase "Way-learning" is the least real.

sentences.zh: 蓋自昔小人殘害良善，率有指名，或以為好名，或以為立異，或以為植黨。

translations.literal: From of old petty men harming the good always had labels—calling them fond of fame, standing apart, forming factions.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men always label the good—fond of fame, standing apart, forming factions.

sentences.zh: 近忽創為『道學』之目，鄭丙唱之，陳賈和之。

translations.literal: Lately they suddenly created the title Way-learning; Zheng Bing initiated it and Chen Jia harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Lately they invented Way-learning; Zheng Bing started it, Chen Jia joined.

sentences.zh: 居要路者密相付授，見士大夫有稍務潔修，粗能操守，輒以道學之名歸之，殆如吃菜事魔、影跡犯敗之類。

translations.literal: Those in key posts secretly transmitted it; seeing gentlemen slightly pure and able to hold integrity, they applied Way-learning—as if vegetable-eating demon worship or shadow-trail crime.
translations.idiomatic: Men in power branded the pure as Way-learning, like demon worship or criminal shadow.

sentences.zh: 往日王淮表裏臺諫，陰廢正人，蓋用此術。

translations.literal: Formerly Wang Huai used censors inside and outside to secretly remove upright men—this technique.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huai used this technique to remove upright men.

sentences.zh: 栗為侍從，無以達陛下之德意志慮，而更襲鄭丙、陳賈密相傳授之說，以道學為大罪。

translations.literal: Li as attendant could not convey Your Majesty's virtue and thought but repeated Zheng and Chen's secret transmission, making Way-learning a great crime.
translations.idiomatic: Li could not convey your virtue but repeated Zheng and Chen, making Way-learning a great crime.

sentences.zh: 文致言語，逐去一熹，固未甚害，第恐自此遊辭無實，讒言橫生，善良受害，無所不有！

translations.literal: Twisting words to drive out one Xi is not very harmful, but I fear from now empty words and slander will arise and the good suffer everywhere!
translations.idiomatic: Driving out Xi alone is small harm, but slander will harm the good everywhere!

sentences.zh: 願陛下正紀綱之所在，絕欺罔於既形，摧抑暴橫以扶善類，奮發剛斷以慰公言。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will rectify discipline, end deceit already formed, suppress violence to support the good, and rouse firm resolve to comfort public opinion.'
translations.idiomatic: Rectify discipline, end deceit, suppress violence, and comfort public opinion.'

sentences.zh: 於是侍御史胡晉臣劾栗，罷之，出知泉州，又改明州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Attendant Censor Hu Jinchen impeached Li; he was dismissed and sent out as prefect of Quanzhou, then Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Jinchen impeached Li; he was dismissed to Quanzhou, then Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 奉祠以卒，諡「簡肅」。

translations.literal: He died holding a sinecure and was given the posthumous title Simple and Stern.
translations.idiomatic: He died in sinecure with posthumous title Simple and Stern.

sentences.zh: 栗為人強介有才，而性狷急，欲快其私忿，遂至攻詆名儒，廢絕師教，殆與鄭丙、陳賈、何澹、劉德秀、劉三傑、胡紘輩黨邪害正者同科。

translations.literal: Li was forceful and talented yet narrow and urgent; wishing to satisfy private resentment he attacked famous scholars and abolished teaching, nearly of the same kind as Zheng Bing, Chen Jia, He Dan, Liu Dexiu, Liu Sanjie, Hu Hong and other faction villains harming the upright.
translations.idiomatic: Li was forceful but narrow; to satisfy private spite he attacked scholars and teaching, ranking with Zheng Bing, Chen Jia, He Dan, and Hu Hong as faction villains.

sentences.zh: 雖疇昔論事，雄辯可觀，不足以蓋晚節之謬也。

translations.literal: Though in former days his discourse was eloquent and worth viewing, it cannot cover the error of his later years.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier eloquence cannot cover his later errors.

sentences.zh: 高文虎

translations.literal: Gao Wenhu
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wenhu

sentences.zh: 高文虎，字炳如，四明人，禮部侍郎閌之從子。

translations.literal: Gao Wenhu, styled Bingru, was a man of Siming, nephew of Vice Minister of Rites Gao Min.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wenhu, courtesy name Bingru, of Siming, was nephew of Vice Minister of Rites Gao Min.

sentences.zh: 登紹興庚辰進士第，調平江府吳興縣主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in gengchen of Shaoxing and was appointed registrar of Wuxing county in Pingjiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in 1160 and became registrar of Wuxing in Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 曾幾守官在吳，文虎從之遊，故聞見博洽，多識典故。

translations.literal: Zeng Ji served there; Wenhu studied with him and therefore had broad hearing and knew many precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Studying under Zeng Ji there, he gained broad learning and knowledge of precedent.

sentences.zh: 除國子正，遷太學博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Rectifier of the Directorate of Education and transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He became rectifier of the Directorate of Education and academy erudite.

sentences.zh: 孝宗幸兩學，祭酒林光朝訪文虎具儀注，文虎輯國朝以來臨幸故事授之。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong visited the two academies, Director Lin Guangchao consulted Wenhu for ritual; Wenhu compiled precedents since the founding for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong visited the academies, Director Lin Guangchao asked Wenhu for ritual precedents since the founding.

sentences.zh: 兼國史院編修官，與修《四朝國史》。

translations.literal: Concurrent Compiler of the National History Academy, he participated in compiling the Four Reigns National History.
translations.idiomatic: As national history compiler he helped compile the Four Reigns National History.

sentences.zh: 出知建昌軍，擢將作丞兼實錄院檢討官，修《高宗實錄》；

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Jianchang, he was promoted to Director of Palace Construction and concurrent Reviewer of the Veritable Records, compiling the Veritable Records of Gaozong;
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Jianchang, he became director of palace construction and veritable records reviewer, compiling Gaozong's Veritable Records;

sentences.zh: 又兼玉牒所檢討官，修《神宗玉牒》。

translations.literal: He was also concurrent Reviewer of the Jade Registers, compiling the Veritable Records of Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: He also reviewed the Jade Registers and compiled Shenzong's Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 自熙寧以來，史氏淆雜，人無所取信。

translations.literal: Since Xining the historians were confused and men had nothing to trust.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xining historians had been confused and untrustworthy.

sentences.zh: 文虎盡取朱墨本刊正繆妄，一一研覈。

translations.literal: Wenhu took all red and black editions to correct errors, examining each one.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhu corrected all editions, examining each item.

sentences.zh: 既奏御，又修《徽宗玉牒》，考訂宣和、崇、觀以來尤為詳審。

translations.literal: After presentation to the throne he also compiled the Veritable Records of Huizong, examining Xuanhe, Chongning, and Guan periods with especial care.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled Huizong's records with especial care for Xuanhe and Chongning.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，遷軍器少監兼將作監，遷國子司業兼學士院權直，遷祭酒、中書舍人，兼直學士院兼祭酒，升實錄院同修撰、同修國史。

translations.literal: When Ningzong ascended he was transferred to Vice Director of the Armory and Palace Construction, then Vice Director of Education and acting Drafter, then Director and Drafting Official, advanced to Associate Compiler of Veritable Records and National History.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ningzong he rose through armory, education, and drafting posts to associate compiler of records and national history.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄用事，既逐趙汝愚、朱熹，以其門多知名士，設偽學之目以擯之，遂命文虎草詔曰：

translations.literal: When Han Tuozhou held power he drove out Zhao Ruyu and Zhu Xi; because their circles had many famous scholars he set up false learning to exclude them and ordered Wenhu to draft an edict saying:
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou expelled Zhao and Zhu, banned false learning, and ordered Wenhu to draft an edict:

sentences.zh: 「向者權臣擅朝，偽邪朋附，協肆姦宄，包藏禍心。

translations.literal: 'Formerly powerful ministers monopolized the court; false and evil cliques attached, conspiring in treachery and harboring evil hearts.
translations.idiomatic: 'Formerly ministers monopolized court; false factions conspired treacherously.

sentences.zh: 賴天之靈，宗廟之福，朕獲承慈訓，膺受內禪，陰謀壞散，國勢復安。

translations.literal: Thanks to Heaven's spirit and the ancestral temple's blessing I received the gentle instruction and undertook internal abdication; secret plots broke up and the state's power was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and the ancestors blessed me to receive abdication; plots collapsed and the state was restored.

sentences.zh: 嘉與士大夫厲精更始，凡曰淫朋比德，幾其自新，而歷載臻茲，弗迪厥化。

translations.literal: I rejoice with gentlemen to reform; all licentious cliques were to renew themselves, yet through the years they have not followed transformation.
translations.idiomatic: I sought reform; licentious cliques were to renew yet have not.

sentences.zh: 締交合盟，窺伺間隙，毀譽舛迕，流言間發，將以傾國是而惑眾心。

translations.literal: They formed alliances and watched for gaps, slandering and contradicting, spreading rumors—intending to overturn state affairs and confuse hearts.
translations.idiomatic: They allied, spread slander and rumors, intending to overturn state affairs.

sentences.zh: 甚至竊附於元祐之眾賢，而不思實類乎紹聖之姦黨。

translations.literal: They even stole attachment to the worthy of Yuanyou yet did not think they truly resembled the villainous faction of Shaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: They posed as Yuanyou worthies yet resembled Shaosheng villains.

sentences.zh: 國家秉德康寧，弗汝瑕殄，今惟自作弗靖，意者漸於流俗之失不可復反歟？

translations.literal: The state bears virtue and peace and does not destroy you; now you make your own disorder—do you gradually fail to return from vulgar error?
translations.idiomatic: The state has spared you; do you refuse to turn from error?

sentences.zh: 將狃于國之寬恩而罰有弗及歟？

translations.literal: Or do you cling to the state's lenient grace while punishment does not reach?
translations.idiomatic: Or do you cling to leniency while punishment spares you?

sentences.zh: 何其未能洗濯以稱朕意也！

translations.literal: How can you fail to wash clean to match my intent!
translations.idiomatic: How can you fail to reform to match my intent!

sentences.zh: 朕既深詔二三大臣與夫侍從言議之官，益維持正論以明示天下矣，諭告所抵，宜各改視回聽，毋復借疑似之說以惑亂世俗。

translations.literal: I have deeply charged great ministers and remonstrance officials to maintain upright discourse and show the realm; where the proclamation reaches, each should change view and listen and not again borrow doubtful talk to confuse society.
translations.idiomatic: I have charged ministers to maintain upright discourse; do not use doubtful talk to confuse society.

sentences.zh: 若其遂非不悔，怙終不悛，邦有常刑，必罰毋赦！」

translations.literal: If they persist in error and stubbornly end without repentance, the state has constant punishment and must punish without pardon!'
translations.idiomatic: Persist in error and constant punishment will not pardon you!'

sentences.zh: 西掖詞命，舊率以數人共一詞，文虎以為非所以崇訓戒、贊人才也，乃人人各為之。

translations.literal: Western Secretariat edicts formerly had several men share one text; Wenhu held that this did not honor admonition and praise talent and had each man write his own.
translations.idiomatic: Western Secretariat edicts were shared; Wenhu had each drafter write separately to honor admonition.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部侍郎兼中書舍人，又兼祭酒，拜翰林學士兼侍讀、實錄院修撰，修國史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War and Drafting Official, again Director, appointed Hanlin Academician and Lecturer and Veritable Records Compiler, compiling National History.
translations.idiomatic: He became war vice minister, drafting official, Hanlin academician, lecturer, and national history compiler.

sentences.zh: 除華文閣學士、知建寧府，力丐祠，提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: Appointed Academician of the Hall for Literary Glory and prefect of Jianning, he strenuously begged a sinecure and was charged with Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Made academician and prefect of Jianning, he begged sinecure at Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 以臺臣言奪職，卒。

translations.literal: On censorial memorial his office was stripped and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Censors stripped his office and he died.

sentences.zh: 文虎以博洽自負，與胡紘合黨，共攻道學，久司學校，專困遏天下士，凡言性命道德者皆絀焉。

translations.literal: Wenhu prided himself on erudition; with Hu Hong he formed a faction attacking Way-learning; long controlling schools he blocked scholars; whoever spoke of fate and morality was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhu prided himself on learning, joined Hu Hong to attack Way-learning, and blocked scholars who spoke of morality.

sentences.zh: 陳自強

translations.literal: Chen Ziqiang
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ziqiang

sentences.zh: 陳自強者，福州閩縣人，字勉之。

translations.literal: Chen Ziqiang was a man of Min county in Fuzhou, styled Mianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ziqiang of Min county, Fuzhou, courtesy name Mianzhi.

sentences.zh: 登淳熙五年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in 1178.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年，入都待銓。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan he entered the capital awaiting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1196 he entered the capital awaiting appointment.

sentences.zh: 自以嘗為韓侂胄童子師，欲見之，無以自通，適僦居主人出入侂胄家，為言於侂胄。

translations.literal: He thought he had once been Han Tuozhou's childhood teacher and wished to see him but had no access; it happened his landlord went in and out of Tuozhou's house and spoke of him to Tuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had been Tuozhou's childhood teacher and wanted an audience; his landlord introduced him.

sentences.zh: 一日，召自強，比至，則從官畢集，侂胄設褥于堂，向自強再拜，次召從官同坐。

translations.literal: One day Tuozhou summoned Ziqiang; when he arrived all attendants were assembled; Tuozhou set a cushion in the hall, bowed again to Ziqiang, then called attendants to sit together.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou summoned him, bowed to him in the hall, and seated attendants with them.

sentences.zh: 侂胄徐曰：「陳先生老儒，汩沒可念。」

translations.literal: Tuozhou slowly said: 'Master Chen is an old scholar; his obscurity is lamentable.'
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou said: 'Master Chen is a neglected old scholar.'

sentences.zh: 明日，從官交薦其才。

translations.literal: The next day attendants jointly recommended his talent.
translations.idiomatic: The next day attendants recommended his talent.

sentences.zh: 除太學錄，遷博士，數月轉國子博士，又遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Recorder of the Imperial Academy, transferred to Erudite, within months to National Erudite, then Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He became academy recorder, erudite, national erudite, then secretary.

sentences.zh: 入館半載，擢右正言、諫議大夫、御史中丞。

translations.literal: Half a year in the Archive he was promoted to Right Rectifier, Remonstrance Grandee, and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year he was censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 入臺未逾月，遂登樞府，由選人至兩地財四年。

translations.literal: Not a month in the censorate he reached the Secretariat—from selector to the two highest posts in four years.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he reached the secretariat—from common appointee to top posts in four years.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰三年，拜右丞相，歷封祁、衛、秦國公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiatai he was appointed Right Chief Councilor, enfeoffed Duke of Qi, Wei, and Qin in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In 1203 he became right chief councilor, enfeoffed duke of Qi, Wei, and Qin.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄顓朝權，包苴盛行，自強尤貪鄙。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou monopolized court power; gifts flourished; Ziqiang was especially greedy and base.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou monopolized power; gifts flourished; Ziqiang was especially greedy.

sentences.zh: 四方致書饋，必題其緘云：「某物並獻」；

translations.literal: Letters and gifts arrived from all sides; he always wrote on the seal: 'Such-and-such item presented together.'
translations.idiomatic: Gifts bore seals reading 'such item presented together.'

sentences.zh: 凡書題無「並」字，則不開。

translations.literal: Any letter lacking the character 'together' he would not open.
translations.idiomatic: Letters without the word 'together' went unopened.

sentences.zh: 縱子弟親戚關通貨賄，仕進干請，必諧價而後予。

translations.literal: He let kin and clients trade bribes and sell offices—only after fixing price would he grant.
translations.idiomatic: Kin sold offices only after fixing price.

sentences.zh: 日押空名刺劄送侂胄家，須用乃填，三省不與也。

translations.literal: Daily he sent blank name-slips to Tuozhou's house to fill when needed; the Three Departments did not see them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent blank appointment slips to Tuozhou's house to fill at need.

sentences.zh: 都城火，自強所貯，一夕為煨燼。

translations.literal: A fire in the capital; Ziqiang's stores were ashes in one night.
translations.idiomatic: A capital fire burned Ziqiang's stores overnight.

sentences.zh: 侂胄首遺之萬緡，執政及列郡聞之，莫不有助。

translations.literal: Tuozhou first gave him ten thousand strings; councilors and prefectures all aided.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou gave ten thousand strings; officials and prefectures aided.

sentences.zh: 不數月，得六十萬緡，遂倍所失之數。

translations.literal: Within months he received six hundred thousand strings—double his loss.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he received six hundred thousand strings—double his loss.

sentences.zh: 創國用司，自為國用使，以費士寅、張岩為同知國用事，掊克民財，州郡騷動。

translations.literal: He created the National Revenue Office, made himself its commissioner with Fei Shiyin and Zhang Yan as associates, squeezing the people's wealth; prefectures were disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He created a revenue office to squeeze wealth and disturb prefectures.

sentences.zh: 方侂胄欲為平章，猶畏眾議，自強首率同列援典故入奏。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou wished to be Grand Councilor but feared public opinion, Ziqiang first led colleagues citing precedent to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuozhou sought grand councilor rank, Ziqiang led colleagues citing precedent.

sentences.zh: 詔以侂胄為平章軍國事。

translations.literal: An edict made Tuozhou Grand Councilor for Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was made grand councilor for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 常語人曰：「自強惟一死以報師王。」

translations.literal: He often told others: 'Ziqiang has only death to repay Teacher King.'
translations.idiomatic: He said he had only death to repay Teacher King.

sentences.zh: 每稱侂胄為恩王、恩父，而呼堂吏史達祖為兄、蘇師旦為叔。

translations.literal: He called Tuozhou Benefactor King and Benefactor Father, called clerk Shi Dazu brother and Su Shidan uncle.
translations.idiomatic: He called Tuozhou benefactor king and father, clerks brother and uncle.

sentences.zh: 侂胄將用兵，遣使北行審敵虛實，自強薦陳景俊以往。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou would use troops he sent envoys north to test the enemy; Ziqiang recommended Chen Jingjun to go.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou sent envoys north; Ziqiang recommended Chen Jingjun.

sentences.zh: 金人有「不宜敗好」之語，景俊歸，自強戒使勿言，侂胄乃決恢復之議。

translations.literal: The Jin said 'peace should not be broken'; Jingjun returned; Ziqiang warned envoys not to speak; Tuozhou then decided on recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Jin envoys said peace must not break; Ziqiang silenced reports; Tuozhou chose war.

sentences.zh: 吳曦有逆謀，求歸蜀，厚賂自強。

translations.literal: Wu Xi had treacherous intent and sought return to Shu, bribing Ziqiang heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi sought return to Shu and bribed Ziqiang.

sentences.zh: 自強語侂胄：「非曦不足以鎮坤維。」

translations.literal: Ziqiang told Tuozhou: 'Only Xi can hold Kunwei.'
translations.idiomatic: Ziqiang said only Xi could hold the west.

sentences.zh: 乃縱之歸，曦卒受金人命為蜀王。

translations.literal: He was allowed to return; Xi ultimately accepted Jin appointment as King of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was allowed back and became Jin king of Shu.

sentences.zh: 侂胄姦凶，久盜國柄，自強實為之表裏。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was treacherous and long usurped power; Ziqiang was truly his inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou usurped power; Ziqiang was his inside man.

sentences.zh: 既開邊隙，朝野洶洶，三遣使請和。

translations.literal: Once the border was opened court and country were alarmed; three missions sought peace.
translations.idiomatic: War alarmed the realm; three missions sought peace.

sentences.zh: 金人欲縛送首議用兵賊臣，侂胄恚憤，復欲用兵，中外大懼。

translations.literal: The Jin wished to hand over the chief war criminals; Tuozhou was furious and wished war again; inside and outside were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Jin demanded war criminals; Tuozhou raged for war again.

sentences.zh: 史彌遠建議誅侂胄，詔以自強阿附充位，不恤國事，罷右丞相。

translations.literal: Shi Miyuan proposed killing Tuozhou; an edict said Ziqiang fawned and filled office without caring for state affairs; he was dismissed as right chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan killed Tuozhou; Ziqiang was dismissed for fawning.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔追三官，永州居住，又責武泰軍節度副使、韶州安置。

translations.literal: Soon he was stripped three ranks and exiled to Yongzhou, then demoted to military vice commissioner at Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped three ranks, exiled to Yongzhou, then Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人倪思繳奏，乞遠竄，籍其家，詔從之。

translations.literal: Drafting Official Ni Si submitted asking farther exile and confiscation; the edict agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Si asked farther exile and confiscation; the edict agreed.

sentences.zh: 再責復州團練副使、雷州安置。

translations.literal: Again demoted to militia vice commissioner at Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again demoted to Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 後死于廣州。

translations.literal: Later he died in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄭丙，字少融，福州長樂人。

translations.literal: Zheng Bing, styled Shaorong, was a man of Changle in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bing of Changle, Fuzhou, courtesy name Shaorong.

sentences.zh: 紹興十五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifteenth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi in 1145.

sentences.zh: 積官至吏部尚書、浙東提舉。

translations.literal: He rose to Minister of Personnel and Zhedong transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of personnel and Zhedong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 朱熹行部至台州，奏台守唐仲友不法事，宰相王淮庇之。

translations.literal: When Zhu Xi toured to Taizhou he memorialized Prefect Tang Zhongyou's illegal conduct; Chief Councilor Wang Huai sheltered him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi memorialized Tang Zhongyou's crimes at Taizhou; Wang Huai sheltered Tang.

sentences.zh: 熹章十上。

translations.literal: Xi submitted ten memorials.
