translations.idiomatic: Xi submitted ten memorials.

sentences.zh: 丙雅厚仲友，且迎合宰相意，奏：「近世士大夫有所謂『道學』者，欺世盜名，不宜信用。」

translations.literal: Bing was thick with Zhongyou and to please the chief councilor memorialized: 'Lately gentlemen have so-called Way-learning, deceiving the age and stealing fame— they should not be trusted.'
translations.idiomatic: Bing, allied with Zhongyou, memorialized that Way-learning deceived the age and should not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 蓋指熹也。

translations.literal: This pointed at Xi.
translations.idiomatic: This targeted Xi.

sentences.zh: 於是監察御史陳賈奏：「道學之徒，假名以濟其偽，乞擯斥勿用。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor Chen Jia memorialized: 'Way-learning followers borrow the name to aid their falsity; beg to exclude and not employ them.'
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Jia asked to exclude Way-learning followers.

sentences.zh: 道學之目，丙倡賈和，其後為慶元學禁，善類被厄，丙罪為多。

translations.literal: The label Way-learning—Bing initiated and Jia harmonized—afterward became the Qingyuan learning ban; the good suffered; Bing's guilt was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Bing started the Way-learning label that became the Qingyuan ban.

sentences.zh: 嘗知泉州，為政暴急，或勸之尚寬，丙曰：「吾疾惡有素，豈以晚節易所守哉。」

translations.literal: He once governed Quanzhou with violent urgency; some urged leniency; Bing said: 'My hatred of evil is of long standing; how can I change what I hold in late years?'
translations.idiomatic: Governing Quanzhou violently, he refused to soften in old age.

sentences.zh: 聞者哂之。

translations.literal: Hearers sneered.
translations.idiomatic: Hearers sneered.

sentences.zh: 丙官終端明殿學士，卒，諡「簡肅」。

translations.literal: Bing ended as Academician of the Duanming Hall, died, posthumous title Simple and Stern.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Duanming academician with posthumous title Simple and Stern.

sentences.zh: 京鏜，字仲遠，豫章人也。

translations.literal: Jing Tang, styled Zhongyuan, was a man of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Tang of Yuzhang, courtesy name Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 登紹興二十七年進士第。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi in 1157.

sentences.zh: 龔茂良帥江西，見之曰：「子廟廓器也。」

translations.literal: Gong Maoliang as Jiangxi commander saw him and said: 'You have the vessel of a temple and altar.'
translations.idiomatic: Gong Maoliang said he had the makings of a state minister.

sentences.zh: 及茂良參大政，遂薦鏜入朝。

translations.literal: When Maoliang entered high government he recommended Tang to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Maoliang rose he recommended Tang.

sentences.zh: 孝宗詔侍從舉良縣令為臺官，給事中王希呂曰：「京鏜蚤登儒級，兩試令，有聲。

translations.literal: Xiaozong ordered attendants to recommend good county magistrates as censors; Drafting Official Wang Xilü said: 'Jing Tang early gained scholarly rank, twice tried as magistrate with reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xilü recommended Tang as censor for his magisterial record.

sentences.zh: 陛下求執法官，鏜其人也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty seeks law-enforcing officials—Tang is the man.'
translations.idiomatic: Tang is the man for enforcing law.'

sentences.zh: 上引見鏜，問政事得失。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Tang and asked the gains and losses of government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Tang and asked policy.

sentences.zh: 時上初統萬機，銳志恢復，群臣進說，多迎合天子意，以為大功可旦暮致。

translations.literal: The emperor had just taken power and was keen on recovery; ministers mostly flattered the Son of Heaven, thinking great merit could come any dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor sought recovery; ministers flattered him that success was near.

sentences.zh: 鏜獨言「天下事未有驟如意者，宜舒徐以圖之」。

translations.literal: Tang alone said: 'Under Heaven nothing suddenly goes as wished; one should proceed slowly to plan.'
translations.idiomatic: Tang alone said nothing succeeds at once; proceed slowly.

sentences.zh: 上善其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 鏜於是極論今日民貧兵驕，士氣頹靡，言甚切至。

translations.literal: Tang then exhaustively discussed today's impoverished people, arrogant troops, and decadent morale, speaking very incisively.
translations.idiomatic: Tang discussed poverty, arrogant troops, and decadent morale incisively.

sentences.zh: 上說，擢為監察御史，累遷右司郎官。

translations.literal: Pleased, the emperor promoted him to Investigating Censor and he rose to Vice Director of the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to investigating censor and right office vice director.

sentences.zh: 金遣賀生辰使來，上居高宗喪，不欲引見，鏜為儐佐，以旨拒之。

translations.literal: The Jin sent birthday felicitation envoys; the emperor was in Gaozong's mourning and did not wish audience; Tang as protocol aide refused on authority.
translations.idiomatic: Jin birthday envoys came during mourning; Tang refused audience.

sentences.zh: 使者請少留闕下，鏜曰：「信使之來，以誕節也。

translations.literal: The envoys asked to stay briefly at the gate; Tang said: 'The faithful envoy comes for the birthday festival.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys asked to linger; Tang said they came only for the birthday rite.

sentences.zh: 誕節禮畢，欲留何名乎？」

translations.literal: When the birthday rite is done, by what name should they stay?'
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ends, by what right should they stay?'

sentences.zh: 使行，上嘉其稱職。

translations.literal: The envoys departed; the emperor praised his fulfilling duty.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys left; the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 轉中書門下省檢正諸房公事。

translations.literal: He transferred to Checking Official of the Secretariat Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He became secretariat checking official.

sentences.zh: 金人遣使來吊，鏜為報謝使。

translations.literal: Jin sent envoys to offer condolences; Tang was returning-thanks envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent condolence envoys; Tang was thanks envoy.

sentences.zh: 金人故事，南使至汴京則賜宴。

translations.literal: Jin custom: southern envoys reaching Bianjing were granted banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Jin custom granted banquets at Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 鏜請免宴，郊勞使康元弼等不從，鏜謂必不免宴，則請徹樂，遺之書曰：「鏜聞鄰喪者舂不相，里殯者不巷歌。

translations.literal: Tang asked to waive banquets; border comfort envoys Kang Yuanyu and others refused; Tang said if banquet unavoidable then beg to remove music, sending a letter:
translations.idiomatic: Tang asked to waive banquets or remove music, citing:

sentences.zh: 今鏜銜命而來，繄北朝之惠吊，是荷是謝。

translations.literal: Tang has heard that at a neighbor's mourning one does not pound grain in unison, and at a lane funeral one does not sing in the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: At a neighbor's mourning one does not pound grain together; at a lane funeral one does not sing.

sentences.zh: 北朝勤其遠而憫其勞，遣郊勞之使，蕆式宴之儀，德莫厚焉，外臣受賜，敢不重拜。

translations.literal: Now Tang bears orders and comes, relying on the northern court's gracious condolence—that is what we bear and thank.
translations.idiomatic: I come relying on the northern court's gracious condolence.

sentences.zh: 若曰而必聽樂，是於聖經為悖理，於臣節為悖義，豈惟貽本朝之羞，亦豈昭北朝之懿哉？」

translations.literal: The northern court labors at distance and pities our toil, sending border-comfort envoys and preparing banquet rites—virtue could not be thicker; this outer subject receiving grace dares not fail to bow deeply.'
translations.idiomatic: Your grace in sending comfort and banquet is great; I dare not fail to bow.'

sentences.zh: 相持甚久。

translations.literal: If you say music must be heard, that is contrary to the sage canon in principle and to ministerial duty in righteousness—is it not shame to our court and does it not obscure your virtue?'
translations.idiomatic: To insist on music violates canon and duty, shaming both courts.'

sentences.zh: 鏜即館，相禮者趣就席，鏜曰：「若不徹樂，不敢即席。」

translations.literal: They contended long.
translations.idiomatic: They contended long.

sentences.zh: 金人迫之，鏜弗為動，徐曰：「吾頭可取，樂不可聞也。」

translations.literal: Tang went to the lodge; ritual officers urged him to seat; Tang said: 'If music is not removed I dare not take seat.'
translations.idiomatic: Tang refused to sit until music ceased.

sentences.zh: 乃帥其屬出館門，甲士露刃向鏜，鏜叱退之。

translations.literal: The Jin pressed him; Tang did not move and slowly said: 'My head may be taken; music may not be heard.'
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by Jin guards, Tang said: 'Take my head, not music.'

sentences.zh: 金人知鏜不可奪，馳白其主，主歎曰：「南朝直臣也。」

translations.literal: He led his attendants out; armored soldiers bared blades at Tang; Tang shouted them down.
translations.idiomatic: Armored soldiers threatened him; he shouted them down.

sentences.zh: 特命免樂。

translations.literal: The Jin knew Tang could not be moved, hurriedly reported to their lord, who sighed: 'The southern court has a straight minister.' A special order waived music.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin ruler called him a straight minister of the southern court and waived music.

sentences.zh: 自是恒去樂而後宴鏜。

translations.literal: From this they always removed music and then banqueted Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth they removed music before banqueting Tang.

sentences.zh: 孝宗聞之喜，謂輔臣曰：「士大夫平居孰不以節義自許，有能臨危不變如鏜者乎？」

translations.literal: Xiaozong heard and rejoiced, telling the chief ministers: 'Which gentleman in normal times does not claim integrity—but who at crisis does not change like Tang?'
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong rejoiced: 'Who at crisis stands firm like Tang?'

sentences.zh: 使還，入見，上勞之曰：「卿能執禮為國家增氣，朕將何以賞卿？」

translations.literal: When the envoy returned and was received, the emperor comforted him: 'You could uphold ritual and add spirit for the state—how shall I reward you?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked how to reward him for upholding ritual.

sentences.zh: 鏜頓首曰：「北人畏陛下威德，非畏臣也。

translations.literal: Tang bowed and said: 'Northerners fear Your Majesty's awe and virtue, not me.
translations.idiomatic: Tang said northerners feared the emperor's virtue, not him.

sentences.zh: 正使臣死於北庭，亦臣子之常分耳，敢言賞乎！」

translations.literal: Even if your servant died in the northern court it is a minister's constant duty—how dare speak of reward!'
translations.idiomatic: Death in the north would be a minister's duty—how dare he ask reward!'

sentences.zh: 故事，使還當增秩。

translations.literal: By precedent returning envoys should gain rank.
translations.idiomatic: Returning envoys normally gained rank.

sentences.zh: 右相周必大言於上曰：「增秩常典爾，京鏜奇節，今之毛遂也，惟陛下念之。」

translations.literal: Right Councilor Zhou Bida said to the emperor: 'Promotion is the constant rule, but Jing Tang's exceptional integrity—today's Mao Sui—only Your Majesty should consider.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bida called Tang today's Mao Sui deserving special notice.

sentences.zh: 乃命鏜權工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was ordered Tang to act as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was made acting vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 四川闕帥，以鏜為安撫制置使兼知成都府。

translations.literal: Sichuan lacked a commander; Tang was made Pacification Commissioner and Concurrent Prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang became Sichuan pacification commissioner and Chengdu prefect.

sentences.zh: 鏜到官，首罷征斂，弛利以予民。

translations.literal: Arriving he first abolished levies and relaxed profits to give the people.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished levies and eased burdens on the people.

sentences.zh: 瀘州卒殺太守，鏜擒而斬之，蜀以大治。

translations.literal: Luzhou soldiers killed the prefect; Tang captured and beheaded them; Shu was greatly governed.
translations.idiomatic: When Luzhou soldiers killed the prefect he executed them and pacified Shu.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，甚見尊禮，由政府累遷為左丞相。

translations.literal: When Ningzong ascended he was greatly honored and from the Secretariat was repeatedly promoted to Left Chief Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ningzong he was honored and rose to left chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 當是時，韓侂胄權勢震天下，其親幸者由禁從不一二歲至宰輔；

translations.literal: At that time Han Tuozhou's power shook the realm; favorites went from palace attendants to chief councilor in one or two years;
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou's power shook the realm; favorites rose to councilor in years;

sentences.zh: 而不附侂胄者，往往沉滯不偶。

translations.literal: those not attached to Tuozhou often stagnated without match.
translations.idiomatic: those not attached stagnated.

sentences.zh: 鏜既得位，一變其素守，於國事謾無所可否，但奉行侂胄風旨而已。

translations.literal: Having gained office Tang wholly changed his former stand; on state affairs he casually neither affirmed nor denied but only followed Tuozhou's intent.
translations.idiomatic: In office Tang abandoned his principles and only followed Tuozhou.

sentences.zh: 又薦引劉德秀排擊善類，於是有偽學之禁。

translations.literal: He also recommended Liu Dexiu to attack the good; thereupon was the false-learning ban.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Liu Dexiu to attack the good, beginning the false-learning ban.

sentences.zh: 後宦者王德謙除節度使，鏜乃請裂其麻，上曰：「除德謙一人而止可乎？」

translations.literal: Later eunuch Wang Deqian was appointed military commissioner; Tang asked to tear up the patent; the emperor said: 'Stopping at Deqian alone—is that acceptable?'
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch was made military commissioner Tang asked to tear up the patent.

sentences.zh: 鏜曰：「此門不可啟。

translations.literal: Tang said: 'This door cannot be opened.
translations.idiomatic: Tang said: 'This door cannot open.

sentences.zh: 節鉞不已，必及三孤；

translations.literal: Military seals do not stop— they must reach the Three Solitaries;
translations.idiomatic: Military seals lead to the Three Solitaries;

sentences.zh: 三孤不已，必及三公。

translations.literal: the Three Solitaries do not stop— they must reach the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: and then to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以真宗不予劉承規為法，以大觀、宣、政間童貫等冒節鉞為戒。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will take as law Zhenzong's not granting Liu Chenggui, and as warning the Tong, Xuan, and Zheng reigns when Tong Guan and others usurped military seals.'
translations.idiomatic: Take Zhenzong's refusal to Liu Chenggui and Tong Guan's usurpation as warnings.'

sentences.zh: 上於是謫德謙而黜詞臣吳宗旦，或曰，亦侂胄意也。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon demoted Deqian and removed drafting official Wu Zongdan—or so it was said, also Tuozhou's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demoted Deqian; some said it was Tuozhou's intent.

sentences.zh: 居無何，以年老請免相，薨，贈太保，諡「文忠」。

translations.literal: Before long, citing age he asked to leave the councilorship, died, posthumous title Literary and Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned for age, died, posthumous title Literary and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 後以監察御史倪千里言，改諡「莊定」。

translations.literal: Later on Censor Ni Qianli's memorial the posthumous title was changed to Settled and Fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ni Qianli later changed his posthumous title to Settled and Fixed.

sentences.zh: 謝深甫

translations.literal: Xie Shenfu
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shenfu

sentences.zh: 謝深甫，字子肅，台州臨海人。

translations.literal: Xie Shenfu, styled Zisu, was a man of Linhai in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shenfu of Linhai, Taizhou, courtesy name Zisu.

sentences.zh: 少穎悟，刻志為學，積數年不寐，夕則置瓶水加足於上，以警困怠。

translations.literal: Young and keen, he carved his will to study; for years he did not sleep; at night he placed a bottle of water on his foot to warn against drowsiness.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied without sleep, placing water on his foot to stay awake.

sentences.zh: 父景之識為遠器，臨終語其妻曰：「是兒當大吾門，善訓迪之。」

translations.literal: His father Jingzhi recognized far-reaching capacity; at death told his wife: 'This boy will enlarge our gate—train him well.'
translations.idiomatic: His father said he would enlarge the family and urged training.

sentences.zh: 母攻苦守志，督深甫力學。

translations.literal: His mother labored bitterly keeping her vow and urged Shenfu to study hard.
translations.idiomatic: His mother urged him to study hard.

sentences.zh: 中乾道二年進士第，調嵊縣尉。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Qiandao; appointed sheriff of Sheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi in 1166; sheriff of Sheng county.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，有死道旁者，一嫗哭訴曰：「吾兒也。

translations.literal: In famine year there was one dead by the road; an old woman cried and complained: 'He is my son.
translations.idiomatic: In famine a woman claimed a roadside corpse was her son.

sentences.zh: 傭於某家，遭掠而斃。」

translations.literal: Hired at a certain house, he was robbed and killed.'
translations.idiomatic: Hired out, he was robbed and killed.'

sentences.zh: 深甫疑焉，徐廉得嫗子他所，召嫗出示之，嫗驚伏曰：「某與某有隙，賂我使誣告耳。」

translations.literal: Shenfu doubted; slowly investigated and found the woman's son elsewhere; summoned the woman and showed him; she knelt in shock: 'I and someone had a grudge; he bribed me to bring false accusation.'
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu found the son alive and exposed a false accusation.

sentences.zh: 越帥方滋、錢端禮皆薦深甫有廊廟才，調昆山丞，為浙曹考官，一時士望皆在選中。

translations.literal: Zhe commander Fang Zi and Qian Duanli both recommended Shenfu had ministerial talent; transferred to Kunshan assistant magistrate; as Zhe examiner all leading scholars of the time were selected.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders recommended him; as examiner he selected leading scholars.

sentences.zh: 司業鄭伯熊曰：「文士世不乏，求具眼如深甫者實鮮。」

translations.literal: Vice Director Zheng Boxiong said: 'Literary men are not lacking in the age; one who seeks discerning eyes like Shenfu is truly rare.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Boxiong said discerning eyes like his were rare.

sentences.zh: 深甫曰：「文章有氣骨，如泰山喬嶽，可望而知，以是得之。」

translations.literal: Shenfu said: 'Writing has bone and spirit like Mount Tai and lofty peaks—visible from afar; that is how I obtained it.'
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu said he chose writing with the bone of great mountains.

sentences.zh: 知處州青田縣。

translations.literal: He governed Qingtian county in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Qingtian in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 侍御史葛邲、監察御史顏師魯、禮部侍郎王藺交薦之。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Ge Qi, Investigating Censor Yan Shilu, and Vice Minister of Rites Wang Lin jointly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and a vice minister recommended him.

sentences.zh: 孝宗召見，深甫言：「今日人才，枵中侈外者多妄誕，矯訐沽激者多眩鬻。

translations.literal: Xiaozong summoned him; Shenfu said: 'Today's talent—many outwardly extravagant and inwardly empty are reckless; many ostentatiously contentious are dazzling peddlers.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned, he warned against flashy, contentious, or merely retiring talent.

sentences.zh: 激昂者急於披露，然或鄰於好誇；

translations.literal: The ardent hurry to expose yet neighbor on boasting;
translations.idiomatic: The ardent risk boasting;

sentences.zh: 剛介者果於植立，而或鄰於太銳；

translations.literal: the rigid and upright are firm in standing yet neighbor on excess sharpness;
translations.idiomatic: the rigid risk excess sharpness;

sentences.zh: 靜退簡默者寡有所合，或鄰於立異。

translations.literal: the quiet and retiring have little agreement yet neighbor on standing apart.
translations.idiomatic: the retiring risk standing apart.

sentences.zh: 故言未及酬而已齟齬，事未及成而已挫抑。

translations.literal: Thus words are not answered before they clash; affairs are not accomplished before they are thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: Words clash before answered; affairs fail before done.

sentences.zh: 於是趣時徇利之人，專務身謀，習為軟熟，畏避束手，因循苟且，年除歲遷，亦至通顯，一有緩急，莫堪倚仗。

translations.literal: Then those who hurry with the times and seek profit specialize in personal schemes, practice softness, fear and bind hands, follow along perfunctorily, advance year by year to prominence—yet in urgency none can be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: Time-servers advance yet cannot be relied on in crisis.

sentences.zh: 臣願任使之際，必察其實，既悉其實，則涵養之以蓄其才，振作之以厲其氣，栽培封殖，勿使沮傷。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that at appointment one must examine reality; having examined, nourish to store talent, rouse to strengthen spirit, cultivate and do not let be discouraged.'
translations.idiomatic: Examine men truly, nourish talent, and do not discourage the able.'

sentences.zh: 上嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted.

sentences.zh: 問當世人才，對曰：「薦士，大臣職也。

translations.literal: Asked about talent of the age he answered: 'Recommending scholars is a great minister's duty.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about talent he said recommendation was ministers' duty.

sentences.zh: 小臣來自遠方，不足以奉明詔。」

translations.literal: This small official comes from afar and is insufficient to serve the bright edict.'
translations.idiomatic: He was too humble to name names.'

sentences.zh: 上頷之，諭宰臣曰：「謝深甫奏對雍容，有古人風。」

translations.literal: The emperor nodded and told the chief ministers: 'Xie Shenfu's memorial reply was composed—he has ancient style.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his ancient style.

sentences.zh: 除籍田令，遷大理丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Altar Fields and transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of altar fields and judicial review assistant.

sentences.zh: 進士俞古應詔言事，語涉詆訐，送瑞州聽讀。

translations.literal: Jinshi Yu Gu memorialized on affairs with words touching slander; he was sent to Ruizhou to hear reading.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi Yu Gu was sent away for harsh memorializing.

sentences.zh: 深甫謂：「以天變求言，未聞旌賞而反罪之，則是名求而實拒也。

translations.literal: Shenfu said: 'Seeking words because of heaven's changes—if reward is not heard but guilt is reversed, then it is named seeking but really refused.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing memorialists while claiming to seek counsel is hypocrisy.

sentences.zh: 俞古不足以道，所惜者朝廷事體耳。」

translations.literal: Yu Gu is insufficient for the Way—what is regretted is the court's manner.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gu matters less than the court's manner.'

sentences.zh: 右司諫鄧馹論近習，左遷，深甫請還馹，謂：「不可以近習故變易諫官，為清朝累。」

translations.literal: Right Office Remonstrator Deng Yi discussed close attendants and was demoted; Shenfu asked to restore Yi, saying: 'One cannot change remonstrance officials because of close attendants and burden the pure court.'
translations.idiomatic: He defended remonstrator Deng Yi demoted for criticizing favorites.

sentences.zh: 二年，知臨安府。

translations.literal: In the second year he governed Lin'an prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he governed Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 三年，除工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 入謝，光宗面諭曰：「京尹寬則廢法，猛則厲民，獨卿為政得寬猛之中。」

translations.literal: Entering thanks Guangzong face-to-face said: 'The capital intendant lenient then law is abandoned, severe then the people suffer—only you govern with both lenient and severe.'
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong praised his balanced rule as capital intendant.

sentences.zh: 進兼吏部侍郎，兼詳定敕令官。

translations.literal: Advanced concurrent Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent Detailed Edict Reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: He became concurrent personnel vice minister and edict reviewer.

sentences.zh: 四年，兼給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was concurrent Drafting Official.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was concurrent drafting official.

sentences.zh: 陳源久以罪斥，忽予內祠，深甫固執不可。

translations.literal: Chen Yuan long banished for crime was suddenly given inner temple post; Shenfu firmly held impossible.
translations.idiomatic: He blocked reinstatement of the banished Chen Yuan.

sentences.zh: 姜特立復詔用，深甫力爭，特立竟不得入。

translations.literal: Jiang Teli was again issued an edict for use; Shenfu strove and Teli ultimately could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: He blocked Jiang Teli's return.

sentences.zh: 張子仁除節度使，深甫疏十一上，命遂寢。

translations.literal: Zhang Ziren was appointed military commissioner; Shenfu memorialized eleven times and the order was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: He blocked Zhang Ziren's military commission with eleven memorials.

sentences.zh: 每禁庭燕私，左右有希恩澤者，上必曰：「恐謝給事有不可耳。」

translations.literal: At each private palace banquet when attendants hoped for grace the emperor always said: 'I fear Drafting Official Xie will not approve.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said he feared Xie would disapprove favors.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，除煥章閣待制、知建康府，改御史中丞兼侍讀。

translations.literal: When Ningzong ascended he was appointed Awaiting Academician of the Hall for Glorifying Culture and prefect of Jiankang, then Censor-in-Chief and Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ningzong he became Jiankang prefect and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 上言：「比年以來，紀綱不立。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'In recent years discipline is not established.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that discipline had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 臺諫有所論擊，不與被論同罷，則反除以外任；

translations.literal: When censors attack, if not dismissed with the accused they are instead transferred outside;
translations.idiomatic: Censors dismissed with the accused or transferred;

sentences.zh: 給、舍有所繳駁，不命次官書行，則反遷以他官；

translations.literal: when drafting officials reject, if the next officer is not ordered to write the line they are instead moved elsewhere;
translations.idiomatic: drafters bypassed or moved;

sentences.zh: 監司有所按察，不兩置之勿問，則被按者反得美除。

translations.literal: when transport officials investigate, if not both set aside the investigated gain fine appointment.
translations.idiomatic: investigators rewarded instead of punished.

sentences.zh: 以奔競得志者，不復知有廉恥；

translations.literal: Those who gain ambition through rushing no longer know shame;
translations.idiomatic: The ambitious forgot shame;

sentences.zh: 以請屬獲利者，不復知有彝憲。

translations.literal: those who gain profit through solicitation no longer know law.
translations.idiomatic: the venal forgot law.

sentences.zh: 貪墨縱橫，莫敢誰何；

translations.literal: Greed and lawlessness run wild—none dare check;
translations.idiomatic: Greed ran wild unchecked;

sentences.zh: 罪惡暴露，無所忌憚。

translations.literal: crimes are exposed—none fear.
translations.idiomatic: crimes went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 隳壞紀綱，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: Destroying discipline—nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 請風厲在位，革心易慮，以肅朝著。」

translations.literal: I beg to stiffen those in office, reform hearts and minds, to rectify the court.'
translations.idiomatic: He begged to stiffen office and rectify the court.'

sentences.zh: 禮官議祧僖祖，侍講朱熹以為不可。

translations.literal: Ritual officials discussed removing Xizu from the temple; Lecturer Zhu Xi held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Ritualists discussed removing Xizu; Zhu Xi objected.

sentences.zh: 深甫言：「宗廟重事，未宜遽革。

translations.literal: Shenfu said: 'Ancestral temple is a weighty matter—not suitable to change hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu said ancestral matters should not be changed hastily.

sentences.zh: 朱熹考訂有據，宜從熹議。」

translations.literal: Xi's examination has basis—follow Xi's proposal.'
translations.idiomatic: Xi's view had basis and should be followed.'

sentences.zh: 嘉泰元年，累疏乞避位，寧宗曰：「卿能為朕守法度，惜名器，不可以言去。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiatai he repeatedly memorialized begging to yield office; Ningzong said: 'You can uphold law and treasure appointments for me—you cannot speak of leaving.'
translations.idiomatic: Begging to resign, he was told he upheld law and could not leave.

sentences.zh: 召坐賜茶，御筆書《說命》中篇及金幣以賜之。

translations.literal: Summoned to sit and given tea; the imperial brush wrote the middle chapter of the Announcement and bestowed gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave tea, wrote from the Announcement, and bestowed gold.

sentences.zh: 有余嚞者，上書乞斬朱熹，絕偽學，且指蔡元定為偽黨。

translations.literal: Yu Yan memorialized begging to behead Zhu Xi, end false learning, and pointed to Cai Yuanding as false faction.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yan asked to behead Zhu Xi and name Cai Yuanding false faction.

sentences.zh: 深甫擲其書，語同列曰：「朱元晦、蔡季通不過自相與講明其學耳，果有何罪乎？

translations.literal: Shenfu threw down the letter and told colleagues: 'Zhu Yuanhui and Cai Jitong only mutually expound their learning—what crime is there?
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu rejected Yu Yan: Zhu and Cai only taught their learning.

sentences.zh: 余嚞蟣蝨臣，乃敢狂妄如此，當相與奏知行遣，以厲其餘。」

translations.literal: Yu Yan is a gnat official yet dares such recklessness—we should jointly memorialize conduct to warn the rest.'
translations.idiomatic: We should punish Yu Yan to warn others.'

sentences.zh: 金使入見不如式，寧宗起入禁中，深甫端立不動，命金使俟於殿隅，帝再御殿，乃引使者進書，迄如舊儀。

translations.literal: When Jin envoys were received without proper form Ningzong rose and entered the inner palace; Shenfu stood upright unmoved, ordering Jin envoys to wait in the hall corner; the emperor again held court and then led the envoy to present the letter—altogether as old ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin envoys broke ritual Shenfu held court form until ritual was restored.

sentences.zh: 許及之

translations.literal: Xu Jizhi
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jizhi

sentences.zh: 許及之，字深甫，溫州永嘉人。

translations.literal: Xu Jizhi, styled Shenfu, was a man of Yongjia in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jizhi of Yongjia, Wenzhou, courtesy name Shenfu.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年第進士，知袁州分宜縣。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the first year of Longxing; governed Fenyi county in Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi in 1163; magistrate of Fenyi in Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 以部使者薦，除諸軍審計，遷宗正簿。

translations.literal: Recommended by the ministry envoy he was appointed Auditor of Various Armies and transferred to Registrar of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as army auditor and clan registrar.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，林栗請增置諫員，乃效唐制置拾遺、補闕，以及之為拾遺，班序在監察御史之上。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao Lin Li asked to add remonstrance officers; following Tang they established Supplementation and Remonstrance, and Jizhi was Supplementation, ranking above Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Li added remonstrance posts, Jizhi became supplementation officer above censors.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，及之言：「皇帝既躬三年之喪，群臣難從純吉，當常服黑帶。」

translations.literal: When Gaozong died Jizhi said: 'The emperor having personally borne three years' mourning, gentlemen find it hard to follow pure auspice— they should constantly wear black bands.'
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozong's death he urged black mourning bands for officials.

sentences.zh: 王淮當國久，及之奏：「陛下即位二十七年，而群臣未能如聖意者，以苟且為安榮，以姑息為仁恕，以不肯任事為簡重，以不敢任怨為老成。

translations.literal: Wang Huai long held the state; Jizhi memorialized: 'Your Majesty has reigned twenty-seven years yet gentlemen cannot match the sage intent because they take perfunctory as peaceful honor, indulgent as humane forgiveness, unwilling to bear affairs as simple weight, and dare not resent blame as seasoned maturity.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Wang Huai's long rule for breeding perfunctory ministers.

sentences.zh: 敢言者指為輕儇，鮮恥者謂之樸實。

translations.literal: Those who dare speak are pointed to as frivolous; those without shame are called plain and real.
translations.idiomatic: Daring speakers were called frivolous; the shameless called plain.

sentences.zh: 陛下得若人而相之，何補於治哉！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty gains such men as councilors, what help to governance!'
translations.idiomatic: Such councilors did not help governance!'

sentences.zh: 淮竟罷職予祠。

translations.literal: Huai was ultimately dismissed and given a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huai was dismissed to a sinecure.

sentences.zh: 光宗受禪，除軍器監，遷太常少卿，以言者罷。

translations.literal: When Guangzong received abdication he was appointed Director of the Armory, transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, dismissed on remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangzong he became armory director and ritual vice director, then was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，除淮南運判兼淮東提刑，以鐵錢濫惡不職，貶秩，知廬州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi he was Huainan transport judge and concurrent Huaidong judicial intendant; for debased iron coins he was demoted in rank and made prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1190 he was demoted for debased iron coins at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 召除大理少卿。

translations.literal: Summoned as Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as judicial review assistant director.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，除吏部尚書兼給事中。

translations.literal: When Ningzong ascended he was Minister of Personnel and Drafting Official.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ningzong he became personnel minister and drafting official.

sentences.zh: 及之早與薛叔似同擢遺、補，皆為當時所予。

translations.literal: Jizhi early with Xue Shusi were together raised as remonstrance and supplementation—both were favored by the time.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xue Shusi had risen together as remonstrance officers.

sentences.zh: 黨事既起，善類一空，叔似累斥逐，而及之謅事侂胄，無所不至。

translations.literal: When faction affairs arose the good were emptied; Shusi was repeatedly expelled while Jizhi fawned on Tuozhou without limit.
translations.idiomatic: When factions arose Shusi was expelled while Jizhi fawned on Tuozhou endlessly.

sentences.zh: 嘗值侂胄生日，朝行上壽畢集，及之後至，閹人掩關拒之，及之俯僂以入。

translations.literal: Once on Tuozhou's birthday after court felicitations all assembled, Jizhi arrived late; eunuchs closed the gate refusing him; Jizhi bowed low to enter.
translations.idiomatic: At Tuozhou's birthday he arrived late and bowed low past closed gates.

sentences.zh: 為尚書，二年不遷，見侂胄流涕，序其知遇之意及衰遲之狀，不覺膝屈。

translations.literal: As minister two years without promotion, seeing Tuozhou he wept, narrating his favor and decline, unconsciously knees bent.
translations.idiomatic: Unpromoted for two years, he wept before Tuozhou and knelt unconsciously.

sentences.zh: 侂胄惻然憐之曰：「尚書才望，簡在上心，行且進拜矣。」

translations.literal: Tuozhou pitied him and said: 'Minister's talent and hope are brief in the sovereign's heart—promotion is coming soon.'
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou pitied him and promised promotion.

sentences.zh: 居亡何，同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Before long he was Associate Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was associate military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 當時有「由竇尚書、屈膝執政」之語，傳以為笑。

translations.literal: At the time there was the saying 'from the hole, Minister; kneeling to govern'—passed as laughter.
translations.idiomatic: People mocked 'from the hole, minister; kneeling to govern.'

sentences.zh: 嘉泰二年，拜參知政事，進知樞密院事兼參政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiatai he was appointed Participant in Governance, advanced to Commissioner of Military Affairs and Participant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1202 he became participant in governance and military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 兵端開，侂胄欲令及之守金陵，及之辭。

translations.literal: When war opened Tuozhou wished Jizhi to guard Jinling; Jizhi declined.
translations.idiomatic: When war opened Tuozhou wanted him to guard Jinling; he declined.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，中丞雷孝友奏及之實贊侂胄開邊，及守金陵，始詭計免行。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou was executed Censor-in-Chief Lei Xiaoyou memorialized that Jizhi truly aided Tuozhou in opening the border; guarding Jinling he began with deceit to avoid going.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Xiaoyou said he aided Tuozhou's war and feigned illness to avoid Jinling.

sentences.zh: 降兩官，泉州居住。

translations.literal: Demoted two ranks and exiled to Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted two ranks and exiled to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉定二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiading he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1209.

sentences.zh: 梁汝嘉

translations.literal: Liang Rujia
translations.idiomatic: Liang Rujia

sentences.zh: 梁汝嘉，字仲謨，處州麗水人。

translations.literal: Liang Rujia, styled Zhongmo, was a man of Lishui in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Rujia of Lishui, Chuzhou, courtesy name Zhongmo.

sentences.zh: 以外祖太宰何執中任入官，調中山府司議曹事。

translations.literal: Through his maternal grandfather Grand Preceptor He Zhizhong's privilege he entered office and was appointed Protocol Officer of Zhongshan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through his grandfather He Zhizhong he entered office at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，知常州武進縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan he was magistrate of Wujin in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianyan's start he was magistrate of Wujin in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 守薦其治狀，擢通判州事，加直秘閣，歷官至轉運副使。

translations.literal: The prefect recommended his governance; he was promoted to Vice Prefect, given Direct Secret Archive, and rose to Vice Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for governance he rose to vice prefect and transport vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 臨安闕守，火盜屢作，命汝嘉攝事。

translations.literal: Lin'an lacked a prefect; fires and bandits occurred repeatedly; Rujia was ordered to act.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an lacked a prefect; Rujia was ordered to act amid fire and bandits.

sentences.zh: 汝嘉修火政，嚴巡徼，盜發輒得，火災亦息。

translations.literal: Rujia repaired fire policy and strict patrols; bandits when active were caught and fires also ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired fire policy and caught bandits.

sentences.zh: 遂命為真，加直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: He was then appointed permanent prefect and given Direct Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He became permanent prefect with Dragon Diagram title.

sentences.zh: 以稱職，擢徽猷閣待制，試戶部侍郎兼知臨安府。

translations.literal: For fulfilling duty he was promoted Awaiting Academician of the Hall for Lofty Principles and tried as Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrent Lin'an prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted for duty he tried as revenue vice minister and Lin'an prefect.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部侍郎，進權尚書兼江、淮、荊、廣經制使。

translations.literal: He rose to Vice Minister of Revenue and advanced Acting Minister concurrent Commissioner for Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Guang circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to acting revenue minister and circuit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 汝嘉素善秦檜，殿中侍御史周葵將按之。

translations.literal: Rujia was always friendly with Qin Hui; Palace Attendant Censor Zhou Kui was about to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: He was friendly with Qin Hui; censor Zhou Kui was to investigate.

sentences.zh: 汝嘉聞，紿中書舍人林待聘曰：「副端將論君。」

translations.literal: Rujia heard and deceived Drafting Official Lin Daipin: 'The vice censor will discuss you.'
translations.idiomatic: He deceived Lin Daipin that Zhou Kui would attack him.

sentences.zh: 待聘亟告檜，徙葵起居郎。

translations.literal: Daipin urgently told Hui; Hui moved Kui to Attendant of the Privy Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Lin told Hui, who moved Kui away.

sentences.zh: 葵入後省，出疏示待聘曰：「梁仲謨何其幸也。」

translations.literal: Kui entered the rear secretariat and showed the memorial to Daipin: 'How fortunate Liang Zhongmo is.'
translations.idiomatic: Kui showed Daipin the memorial: 'How fortunate for Liang.'

sentences.zh: 待聘始知為汝嘉所賣，士大夫以是薄汝嘉。

translations.literal: Daipin then knew he was sold by Rujia; gentlemen therefore despised Rujia.
translations.idiomatic: Daipin knew Rujia had sold him; gentlemen despised Rujia.

sentences.zh: 汝嘉求去，以寶文閣直學士提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: Rujia asked to leave; made Direct Academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture charged with Taiping Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for Taiping Observatory.

sentences.zh: 未幾，升學士、知明州，兼浙西沿海制置使，更溫、宣、鼎三郡，復奉祠以歸。

translations.literal: Before long advanced academician and prefect of Mingzhou, concurrent Zhexi coastal commissioner, then Wen, Xuan, and Ding—three prefectures—and again sinecure and home.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Mingzhou and three prefectures, then retired.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Shaoxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1153.

sentences.zh: 汝嘉長於吏治，在臨安風績尤著。

translations.literal: Rujia was skilled in administration; at Lin'an his achievements were especially notable.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in administration, especially at Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 論曰：君子之論人，亦先觀其大者而已矣。

translations.literal: The gentleman judging men also first observes the great points.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: judging men begins with the great points.

sentences.zh: 忠孝，人之大節也，胡紘導其君以短喪，不得謂之忠；

translations.literal: Loyalty and filial piety are man's great bonds; Hu Hong led his ruler to short mourning—he cannot be called loyal;
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and filial piety are great bonds; Hu Hong led his ruler to short mourning—not loyal;

sentences.zh: 何澹疑所生繼母之服，士論紛紜而後去，不可以為孝。

translations.literal: He Dan doubted mourning for birth mother who was stepmother; gentlemen disputed and only then left—he cannot be called filial.
translations.idiomatic: He Dan doubted stepmother mourning—not filial.

sentences.zh: 彼於其大者且忍為之，則其協比權姦，誣構善類，亦何憚而不為乎？

translations.literal: When they could bear such on the great points, then joining powerful villains and framing the good—what would they fear not to do?
translations.idiomatic: Having failed the great bonds, they feared nothing in joining villains.

sentences.zh: 謝深甫出處，舊史泯其跡，若無可議為者。

translations.literal: Xie Shenfu's coming and going—the old history blurs his traces as if nothing to criticize.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shenfu's record seems blameless.

sentences.zh: 然慶元之初，韓侂胄設偽學之禁，網羅善類而一空之，深甫秉政，適與之同時，諉曰不知，不可也。

translations.literal: Yet at the beginning of Qingyuan Han Tuozhou set the false-learning ban, netting the good and emptying them; Shenfu held office exactly at the same time—saying he did not know cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: Yet during the false-learning ban Shenfu held office—pleading ignorance fails.

sentences.zh: 況于一劾陳傅良，再劾趙汝愚，形於深甫之章，有不可揜者乎？

translations.literal: Moreover impeaching Chen Fuliang once and Zhao Ruyu twice appears in Shenfu's memorials—can it be covered?
translations.idiomatic: His memorials impeached Chen Fuliang and twice impeached Zhao Ruyu.

sentences.zh: 陳自強、鄭丙、許及之輩，狐媚苟合，以竊貴寵，斯亦不足論已。

translations.literal: Chen Ziqiang, Zheng Bing, Xu Jizhi and their kind—fawning and base to steal honor—are not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ziqiang, Zheng Bing, and Xu Jizhi are not worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 若林栗之有治才，善論事，高文虎之自負該洽，京鏜之仗義秉禮，志信於敵國，抑豈無足稱者。

translations.literal: Yet if Lin Li had governing talent and was good at discourse, Gao Wenhu prided himself on comprehensive learning, Jing Tang upheld righteousness and ritual with faith before the enemy state—are there not points worth praising?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lin Li governed well, Wenhu was learned, Tang upheld ritual before enemies—were they without merit?

sentences.zh: 然栗以私忿詆名儒，不為清議所與，而文虎草偽學之詔，以是為非，以正為邪，變亂白黑，以欺當世，其人可知也。

translations.literal: Yet Li from private resentment slandered famous scholars and was not given by pure opinion; Wenhu drafted the false-learning edict—therefore wrong was taken as right and white and black were reversed to deceive the age; such men can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li slandered scholars; Wenhu drafted the false-learning edict and reversed right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 鏜暮年得政，朋姦取容，既愧其初服矣，況偽學之目，識者以為鏜實發之乎？

translations.literal: Tang in late years gained office and fawned on villains, already shaming his first intent—how much more the false-learning label, which discerning men think Tang actually initiated?
translations.idiomatic: Tang in old age fawned on villains; some say he started the false-learning label.

sentences.zh: 士君子立身行事，一失其正，流而不知返，遂為千古之罪人，可不懼哉！

translations.literal: The gentleman establishing body and acting—once losing the upright, flowing without knowing return, then becoming a criminal through the ages—can one not fear!
translations.idiomatic: Once a gentleman loses the upright path he becomes an age's criminal—should we not fear!

sentences.zh: 可不懼哉！

translations.literal: Can one not fear!
translations.idiomatic: Should we not fear!
